questions.prompt: A nurse is preparing to administer a bronchodilator to a client with asthma. Which of the following outcomes would indicate that the medication has been effective?
options: The client's pulse oximetry reading is 92%
The client is able to speak in full sentences
The client's respiratory rate is 20 breaths per minute
The client's peak flow reading has decreased
questions.rationale: The ability to speak in full sentences without becoming short of breath indicates that the bronchodilator is effective and the client's airway obstruction is improving.

questions.prompt: A patient with asthma has a peak flow reading that is 50% of their personal best. Which of the following actions should the nurse take?
options: Encourage the patient to rest and continue monitoring
Administer a bronchodilator
Increase the oxygen flow rate
Prepare for endotracheal intubation
questions.rationale: A peak flow reading that is 50% of the personal best indicates a severe decrease in lung function. The nurse should administer a bronchodilator to help open the airways and improve breathing.

questions.prompt: A patient with asthma is prescribed a short-acting beta2-agonist and a glucocorticoid inhaler. Which medication should the nurse instruct the patient to use first?
options: The beta2-agonist
The glucocorticoid
Either can be used first
Neither, they should be used simultaneously
questions.rationale: The short-acting beta2-agonist should be used first to dilate the bronchioles and improve airflow. This will then enhance the distribution and absorption of the glucocorticoid inhaler.

questions.prompt: A patient with asthma has been prescribed a metered-dose inhaler (MDI). What instruction should the nurse provide to the patient about using the MDI?
options: Inhale quickly and deeply
Exhale fully before using the MDI
Hold the breath for 10 seconds after inhaling the medication
All of the above
questions.rationale: All of these instructions are correct and help ensure the medication is inhaled into the lungs effectively.

questions.prompt: A patient is admitted to the emergency department with severe difficulty breathing, cyanosis, and a respiratory rate of 40 breaths per minute. The nurse notes absent breath sounds on the left side of the chest. What should the nurse do next?
options: Administer a bronchodilator
Prepare the patient for chest tube insertion
Administer supplemental oxygen
Initiate cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR)
questions.rationale: The patient's symptoms suggest a tension pneumothorax, a life-threatening condition that requires immediate decompression with chest tube insertion.

questions.prompt: A nurse is caring for a patient who is 2 days post-op from a thoracotomy. The patient is reluctant to perform deep breathing exercises due to pain. Which of the following interventions should the nurse implement?
options: Administer pain medication before the exercises
Encourage shallow breathing to prevent discomfort
Discontinue the exercises until the pain subsides
Encourage the patient to hold their breath as long as possible
questions.rationale: Deep breathing exercises are critical after thoracotomy to prevent complications such as pneumonia and atelectasis. Administering pain medication before the exercises can help alleviate the patient's discomfort and encourage compliance.

questions.prompt: A patient with asthma has been prescribed a corticosteroid inhaler and a bronchodilator inhaler. How should these medications be administered?
options: The bronchodilator should be used, followed by the corticosteroid
The corticosteroid should be used, followed by the bronchodilator
Both inhalers should be used simultaneously
The order of administration does not matter
questions.rationale: The bronchodilator should be administered first to open the airways, allowing the corticosteroid to be more effectively delivered and absorbed.

questions.prompt: A nurse is caring for a patient with pneumonia. The nurse notes decreased breath sounds in the lower lobes of both lungs. What should the nurse anticipate?
options: Administering a bronchodilator
Initiating oxygen therapy
Performing chest physiotherapy
Assisting with endotracheal intubation
questions.rationale: Decreased breath sounds in the bases of the lungs indicate mucus accumulation, which can be mobilized with chest physiotherapy.

questions.prompt: A patient is admitted with a diagnosis of pulmonary embolism. What is the priority nursing intervention for this patient?
options: Administer anticoagulants as ordered
Encourage ambulation
Provide supplemental oxygen
Monitor vital signs
questions.rationale: The immediate priority for a patient with a pulmonary embolism is to improve oxygenation, which can be achieved by providing supplemental oxygen.

questions.prompt: A patient with pneumonia has a decreased level of consciousness and is at risk for aspiration. Which of the following interventions would be most appropriate for this patient?
options: Place the patient in a supine position
Administer oxygen via nasal cannula
Use a spacer with metered-dose inhalers
Position the patient on their side
questions.rationale: A side-lying position can help prevent aspiration by allowing secretions to drain from the mouth. The other options would not specifically address the risk for aspiration in this patient.

Ask the UAP to assist the client to ambulate in the hallway.
Elevate the head of the bed, assess airway/lung sounds, and apply supplemental oxygen.

questions.prompt: A mechanically ventilated patient has a respiratory rate of 35 breaths per minute. The ventilator is set to deliver 12 breaths per minute. What action should the nurse take?
options: Increase the ventilator rate to match the patient's rate
Sedate the patient to decrease the respiratory rate
Assess the patient for causes of increased respiratory rate
Notify the physician
questions.rationale: The patient may be breathing above the ventilator rate due to hypoxia, pain, anxiety, or other reasons. The nurse should assess the patient to identify and address the cause.

questions.prompt: A nurse is caring for a patient with pneumonia. Which of the following interventions should the nurse prioritize?
options: Encourage ambulation
Administer antibiotics as prescribed
Maintain a patent airway
Promote fluid intake
questions.rationale: Maintaining a patent airway is the priority nursing intervention for a patient with pneumonia because pneumonia can cause mucus production that can obstruct the airway.

questions.prompt: The nurse is caring for a patient with a tracheostomy. Which of the following instructions should the nurse provide to the patient to prevent complications?
options: Limit fluid intake
Avoid humidified environments
Perform tracheostomy care daily
Encourage coughing and deep breathing
questions.rationale: Regular coughing and deep breathing exercises can help to clear secretions from the lungs and maintain a patent airway, reducing the risk of complications such as pneumonia.

questions.prompt: A nurse is caring for a patient with a respiratory rate of 6 breaths per minute. The patient is lethargic and unresponsive. Which of the following actions should the nurse take?
options: Administer oxygen
Position the patient on their side
Prepare for intubation
Initiate CPR
questions.rationale: A respiratory rate of 6 breaths per minute is dangerously low and indicates respiratory failure. The patient is unresponsive, suggesting a lack of oxygen to the brain. Immediate intervention, such as intubation, is needed.

questions.prompt: A nurse is caring for a client who has a tracheostomy. Which of the following interventions should the nurse include in the plan of care?
options: Provide tracheostomy care every shift
Use sterile technique when suctioning the tracheostomy
Encourage the client to cough and deep breathe every 2 hours
All of the above
questions.rationale: All the listed interventions are part of the appropriate care for a client with a tracheostomy. They all help maintain a patent airway, promote effective gas exchange, and prevent infection.

questions.prompt: A nurse is caring for a patient who suddenly becomes restless and anxious, with increased heart rate and decreased oxygen saturation. The nurse assesses decreased breath sounds on the right side of the chest. What should the nurse do next?
options: Administer a bronchodilator
Notify the physician immediately
Increase the rate of IV fluids
Position the patient on the left side
questions.rationale: These symptoms suggest a pneumothorax, a medical emergency. The nurse should notify the physician immediately for further intervention.

questions.prompt: A client managed for COPD, Asthma, Pneumonia, Pulmonary Embolism & ARDS develops sudden tachypnea (RR 32/min), SpO2 87%, and new-onset restlessness. What should the nurse do FIRST?
options: Ask the UAP to assist the client to ambulate in the hallway.
Administer a PRN opioid analgesic for restlessness before assessing.
Elevate the head of the bed, assess airway/lung sounds, and apply supplemental oxygen.
Document the vital signs and recheck oxygen saturation in 2 hours.

questions.prompt: A nurse is caring for a patient with a diagnosis of emphysema. Which of the following clinical manifestations would be expected?
options: Increased breath sounds
Decreased anterior-posterior diameter
Prolonged expiration
Cyanosis
questions.rationale: Emphysema is characterized by prolonged expiration due to loss of elastic recoil and air trapping in the lungs.

options: Decreased respiratory rate
Increased sputum production
Decreased oxygen saturation
Increased breath sounds
questions.rationale: A decrease in respiratory rate following a nebulizer treatment can indicate that the medication has helped to open the airways, making it easier for the patient to breathe.

questions.prompt: A client with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) is experiencing shortness of breath. What position should the nurse instruct the patient to assume to facilitate breathing?
options: Supine
Prone
High Fowler's
Trendelenburg
questions.rationale: The High Fowler's position, sitting up at 90 degrees, allows for maximum lung expansion and can help improve oxygenation in a patient with COPD.

questions.prompt: A patient with pneumonia is having difficulty breathing. Which position would be most beneficial for this patient?
options: Supine
Prone
High Fowler's
Trendelenburg
questions.rationale: The High Fowler's position allows for maximum lung expansion and can assist in improving oxygenation for a patient with pneumonia.

questions.prompt: A patient with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) has been admitted to the hospital. Which of the following findings would the nurse expect to observe during the assessment?
options: Decreased respiratory rate
Prolonged expiratory phase
Increased lung sounds
Absence of wheezing
questions.rationale: Patients with COPD often have difficulty exhaling, leading to a prolonged expiratory phase. The other options are not typical findings in COPD.

questions.prompt: A nurse cares for a client presenting with Tension Pneumothorax (Respiratory Medications: Bronchodilators, Steroids & Anti-TB Regimens). What is the priority nursing action?

questions.prompt: A client is prescribed a bronchodilator and a corticosteroid inhaler for treatment of asthma. Which of the following should the nurse instruct the client to do?
options: Use the corticosteroid inhaler first
Use the bronchodilator first
Use both inhalers at the same time
It does not matter which inhaler is used first
questions.rationale: The bronchodilator should be used first to open up the airways, allowing the corticosteroid inhaler to be more effective.

questions.prompt: A nurse is caring for a patient with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD). Which of the following is the most common sign of hypoxemia in this patient?
options: Tachycardia
Tachypnea
Confusion
Cyanosis
questions.rationale: In patients with COPD, the most common sign of hypoxemia is not cyanosis, tachycardia, or tachypnea, but rather acute confusion or subtle personality changes due to decreased oxygen supply to the brain.

questions.prompt: A nurse is caring for a patient who is experiencing dyspnea and is diagnosed with pulmonary edema. Which of the following actions should the nurse prioritize?
options: Position the patient in a high Fowler’s position.
Encourage deep breathing and coughing.
Auscultate lung sounds bilaterally.
Administer prescribed diuretics.
questions.rationale: The high Fowler's position reduces venous return to the heart, thereby decreasing pulmonary congestion and improving the patient's breathing.

questions.prompt: A nurse is caring for a patient with asthma. Which of the following assessments would indicate an impending asthma attack?
options: Decreased wheezing
Increased peak flow rate
Sudden restlessness and anxiety
Decreased pulse rate
questions.rationale: A sudden change in behaviour, such as increased restlessness and anxiety, can indicate hypoxia, which could be a sign of an impending asthma attack.

questions.prompt: A nurse is caring for a patient post bronchoscopy. Which of the following is the most important assessment before offering the patient food or drink?
options: Vital signs
Oxygen saturation
Level of consciousness
Return of the gag reflex
questions.rationale: After a bronchoscopy, the patient’s throat may be numb from local anaesthetics used during the procedure. It is essential to ensure the return of the gag reflex before offering food or drink to prevent aspiration.

questions.prompt: A nurse is caring for a patient with pneumonia who is receiving supplemental oxygen. What would be the best way to evaluate the effectiveness of the oxygen therapy?
options: Pulse oximetry
Arterial blood gas analysis
Respiratory rate
Blood pressure
questions.rationale: Arterial blood gas analysis provides the most accurate information about the patient's oxygenation status and the effectiveness of oxygen therapy.

questions.prompt: A nurse is caring for a patient with tuberculosis. Which of the following actions should the nurse take to prevent the spread of the disease?
options: Wear a mask when providing direct patient care
Place the patient in a private room
Wash hands after removing gloves
All of the above
questions.rationale: Tuberculosis is an airborne disease. It is crucial to wear a mask, place the patient in a private room, and wash hands after removing gloves to prevent the spread of the disease.

questions.prompt: A client managed for Respiratory Medications: Bronchodilators, Steroids & Anti-TB Regimens develops sudden tachypnea (RR 32/min), SpO2 87%, and new-onset restlessness. What should the nurse do FIRST?
options: Elevate the head of the bed, assess airway/lung sounds, and apply supplemental oxygen.
Document the vital signs and recheck oxygen saturation in 2 hours.
Ask the UAP to assist the client to ambulate in the hallway.
Administer a PRN opioid analgesic for restlessness before assessing.
questions.rationale: Under Maslow's hierarchy and ABC prioritization in Respiratory Medications: Bronchodilators, Steroids & Anti-TB Regimens, airway and oxygenation cues (SpO2 87%, RR 32, hypoxia-induced restlessness) require immediate airway/O2 support first.

questions.prompt: A patient on a ventilator is experiencing a decrease in oxygen saturation. The nurse increases the fraction of inspired oxygen (FiO2) but the saturation does not improve. What should the nurse do next?
options: Increase the respiratory rate on the ventilator
Administer a bronchodilator
Perform endotracheal suctioning
Increase the positive end-expiratory pressure (PEEP)
questions.rationale: The nurse should next perform endotracheal suctioning to clear any secretions that might be obstructing the airway and affecting oxygenation. If this does not improve oxygenation, other interventions such as increasing PEEP may be considered.

questions.prompt: A nurse cares for a client presenting with Chest Tube (Water-Seal) (COPD, Asthma, Pneumonia, Pulmonary Embolism & ARDS). What is the priority nursing action?
options: Continuous gentle bubbling in suction chamber = normal; tidaling in water seal = normal.
Wait 4 hours to reassess before taking any action or documenting.
Delegate acute clinical assessment and teaching to UAP/CNA.
Administer sedatives or diuretics without reviewing baseline labs or vitals.
questions.rationale: For Chest Tube (Water-Seal), the priority intervention is: Continuous gentle bubbling in suction chamber = normal; tidaling in water seal = normal. Key exam watchpoint: Intermittent bubbling is OK; continuous bubbling in water seal = air leak. If dislodged, tape 3 sides!

questions.prompt: A nurse is educating a patient with COPD about the use of a metered-dose inhaler (MDI) with a spacer. Which of the following instructions should the nurse include?
options: Exhale completely before activating the MDI
Inhale quickly and forcefully through the spacer
Hold breath for 5 seconds after inhaling the medication
Rinse mouth with water immediately after using the MDI
questions.rationale: The patient should exhale completely to empty the lungs as much as possible before inhaling the medication. This allows for maximum distribution of the medication in the lungs.

questions.prompt: A nurse is preparing to administer albuterol to a patient with asthma. Which of the following should the nurse monitor for as a potential side effect of this medication?
options: Bradycardia
Hypotension
Tachycardia
Hypoglycaemia
questions.rationale: Albuterol, a beta2-adrenergic agonist, can cause tachycardia as a side effect. It stimulates the beta2 receptors in the lungs causing bronchodilation, but it can also stimulate beta1 receptors in the heart causing increased heart rate.

questions.prompt: A nurse is caring for a 6-month-old infant with Down syndrome. Which of the following interventions should be included in the nursing care plan?
options: Limit physical activity to prevent overexertion
Encourage regular, age-appropriate developmental stimulation
Restrict social interaction to prevent overstimulation
Avoid discussing the diagnosis with the family
questions.rationale: Correct answer: Encourage regular, age-appropriate developmental stimulation (Verified from PAEDIATRIC QUESTIONS.docx and Saunders 9th Ed.).

questions.prompt: A patient with pheochromocytoma is experiencing hypertension and tachycardia. What is the primary goal of treatment?
options: Decrease catecholamine production
Increase catecholamine production
Regulate blood pressure
Reduce tumor size
questions.rationale: Reducing catecholamine levels controls blood pressure.

questions.prompt: Question: A nurse is providing psychosocial support to a patient with hearing loss. Which of the following actions should the nurse take?
options: Encourage the patient to isolate from social activities
Promote the use of sign language
Avoid discussing feelings about hearing loss
Ignore the patient's frustration about the condition
questions.rationale: Correct answer: Promote the use of sign language (Verified from eye and ear  QNS.docx and Saunders 9th Ed.).

questions.prompt: A nurse is caring for a patient who has a tracheostomy. Which of the following interventions would the nurse include in the plan of care to prevent a common complication associated with a tracheostomy?
options: Frequent oral care
Encourage ambulation
Turn the patient every 2 hours
Provide a high protein diet
questions.rationale: Frequent oral care helps to prevent infections, a common complication associated with a tracheostomy.

questions.prompt: A 12-year-old child weighing 50 kg is ordered a medication at a dose of 5 mg/kg/day in 3 divided doses. How many milligrams of the medication will the nurse administer per dose?
options: 30 mg
50 mg
75 mg
83 mg
questions.rationale: Correct answer: 83 mg (Verified from PAEDIATRIC QUESTIONS.docx and Saunders 9th Ed.).

questions.prompt: A nurse is preparing to administer an intramuscular (IM) injection to a 1-year-old child. Which site should the nurse select?
options: Deltoid
Ventrogluteal
Vastus Lateralis
Dorsogluteal
questions.rationale: Correct answer: Vastus Lateralis (Verified from PAEDIATRIC QUESTIONS.docx and Saunders 9th Ed.).

questions.prompt: A nurse is caring for a patient who is scheduled for a corneal transplant. Which of the following is a key preoperative responsibility of the nurse?
options: Administering preoperative antibiotics
Ensuring the patient has a clear understanding of the procedure
Verifying that the patient has arranged for help at home after discharge
All of the above
questions.rationale: All of these actions are important nursing responsibilities before a corneal transplant. The patient should understand the procedure, any risks, and postoperative care, have preoperative antibiotics to prevent infection, and ensure they have arranged for help at home postoperatively as vision may be impaired.

questions.prompt: A patient is admitted with a pulmonary embolism. Which of the following is the priority nursing intervention?
options: Administer anticoagulant therapy as ordered
Provide supplemental oxygen
Monitor vital signs
Encourage ambulation
questions.rationale: The immediate priority for a patient with a pulmonary embolism is to improve oxygenation, which can be achieved by providing supplemental oxygen.

questions.prompt: The parents of a 2-year-old child with short bowel syndrome are concerned about their child's nutrition. Which of the following is an appropriate recommendation by the nurse?
options: The child should consume a high-fiber diet.
The child may require parenteral nutrition.
The child should avoid all fats in the diet.
The child should consume more dairy products.
questions.rationale: Short bowel syndrome can lead to malabsorption of nutrients. In severe cases, parenteral nutrition may be required to ensure the child receives adequate nutrition. A high-fiber diet (option A) may not be appropriate as it can increase stool output. Avoiding all fats (option C) is not recommended as some fat is necessary for growth and development. While some children with short bowel syndrome may tolerate dairy products (option D), others may not due to lactose intolerance.

questions.prompt: During auscultation of the lungs, the nurse hears a course, low-pitched bubbling sound during inspiration and expiration. What could this indicate?
options: Normal lung sounds
Pneumonia
Asthma
Emphysema
questions.rationale: The sound described is known as crackles, which can signify pneumonia. Crackles are caused by the sudden opening of small airways and alveoli collapsed by fluid, exudate, or lack of aeration during expiration.

questions.prompt: A nurse is providing discharge instructions to the parents of a child who has undergone chemotherapy. Which of the following instructions should be included?
options: "Your child should avoid crowds and people with infections."
"Your child can return to school and engage in physical activities."
"Your child should eat a diet high in raw fruits and vegetables."
"Your child can receive live virus vaccines."
questions.rationale: Children who have undergone chemotherapy have a suppressed immune system and are more susceptible to infections. They should avoid crowds and people with infections to minimize the risk of getting sick.

questions.prompt: A nurse is caring for a client with a hearing impairment. Which of the following interventions should the nurse implement to promote effective communication?
options: Speak loudly and over-enunciate each word
Maintain direct eye contact and speak in a normal tone
Speak to the client from behind to reduce distractions
Use complex medical terminologies to explain the condition
questions.rationale: Correct answer: Maintain direct eye contact and speak in a normal tone (Verified from eye and ear  QNS.docx and Saunders 9th Ed.).

questions.prompt: The nurse is caring for a 4-year-old child who has been prescribed ear drops for an ear infection. How should the nurse administer the medication?
options: By pulling the earlobe up and back.
By pulling the earlobe down and back.
By inserting the dropper into the ear canal.
By having the child lie on his stomach.
questions.rationale: Correct answer: By pulling the earlobe down and back. (Verified from PAEDIATRIC QUESTIONS.docx and Saunders 9th Ed.).

questions.prompt: A 5-year-old child is diagnosed with leukemia and is about to start chemotherapy. Which of the following nursing interventions is a priority?
options: Teaching the child about the side effects of chemotherapy
Providing emotional support to the child and the family
Administering anti-emetic medication as ordered
Ensuring the child is given a balanced diet
questions.rationale: While all these options are important in the care of a child with leukemia, the priority intervention is to provide emotional support to the child and the family. This is due to the significant emotional impact that a cancer diagnosis can have on the child and the family.

questions.prompt: Which of the following symptoms should the nurse expect to find in a client diagnosed with right-sided heart failure?
options: Crackles in the lungs
Peripheral edema
Productive cough
Orthopnoea
questions.rationale: Right-sided heart failure results in systemic congestion, which manifests as peripheral edema. Crackles in the lungs, productive cough, and orthopnea are associated with left-sided heart failure due to pulmonary congestion.

questions.prompt: A nurse is caring for a patient on a ventilator. The high-pressure alarm on the ventilator sounds. Which of the following could be a possible cause?
options: The client is biting on the endotracheal tube
The ventilator is disconnected
The client has a high respiratory rate
There is an increased oxygen demand
questions.rationale: The high-pressure alarm may be triggered by anything that increases airway resistance, such as biting on the endotracheal tube, excessive secretions, or bronchospasm.

questions.prompt: A nurse is delegating tasks to a nursing assistant on a pediatric oncology unit. Which task is appropriate to delegate?
options: Discussing the side effects of chemotherapy with a patient's parents
Administering oral pain medication to a child with bone cancer
Assisting a child with leukemia with bathing and dressing
Assessing a child's response to a blood transfusion
questions.rationale: Option C is an appropriate task to delegate to a nursing assistant as it falls within their scope of practice. Options A, B, and D involve patient education, medication administration, and assessment, respectively, which are within the nurse's scope of practice and should not be delegated.

blocks.title: Insulin Profiles & Peak Hypoglycemia Watch Times
rows: **Rapid-Acting** (Lispro, Aspart, Glulisine)
**1 – 3 hours**
Give only when meal tray is **in front of client**!
**Short-Acting** (Regular — Humulin R)
**2 – 4 hours**
ONLY insulin safe for **IV push/drip (DKA)**; draw clear before cloudy (RN).
**Intermediate** (NPH — Cloudy)
1 – 2 hours
Roll gently between palms (do not shake); risk for afternoon/evening low glucose.
**Long-Acting** (Glargine, Detemir)
1 – 2 hours
**Peakless (No pronounced peak)**
Do **NOT mix** in same syringe with any other insulin; give once daily same time.

rows: **Thyroid Storm vs. Myxedema**
**Storm:** Fever > 104°F, HR > 140, delirium. **Myxedema:** Hypothermia, bradycardia, coma.
**Storm:** PTU, iodine, beta-blockers, cooling (NO aspirin!). **Myxedema:** IV Levothyroxine + warming.
**Addison's vs. Cushing's**
**Addison (Low steroid):** Hypotension, hyperkalemia, bronze skin. **Cushing (High):** Moon face, hyperglycemia, K+ loss.
**Addisonian Crisis:** Rapid IV 0.9% NS + **IV Hydrocortisone**; never stop chronic steroids abruptly.
**SIADH vs. Diabetes Insipidus**
**SIADH (High ADH):** Fluid overload, hyponatremia, high urine SG. **DI (Low ADH):** Polyuria, hypernatremia, low urine SG (<1.005).
**SIADH:** Fluid restriction + 3% NS if seizures. **DI:** Desmopressin (DDAVP) + IV fluids.

items: Integrate Addison's vs. Cushing's Disease, SIADH & Diabetes Insipidus cues across the 6-Step NCSBN CJMM: Recognize -> Analyze -> Prioritize -> Generate -> Act -> Evaluate.
Compare US Conventional lab values (mg/dL, mEq/L) and US generic drug names (Acetaminophen, Epinephrine, Albuterol) before choosing an option.
Verify mastery of Addison's vs. Cushing's Disease, SIADH & Diabetes Insipidus using the 20-question topic quiz and the Course Unit 6 60-question mixed Final Evaluation.

options: Elevate the head of the bed, assess airway/lung sounds, and apply supplemental oxygen.
Document the vital signs and recheck oxygen saturation in 2 hours.
Administer a PRN opioid analgesic for restlessness before assessing.
Ask the UAP to assist the client to ambulate in the hallway.
questions.rationale: Under Maslow's hierarchy and ABC prioritization in Hypothyroidism, Hyperthyroidism (Thyroid Storm) & Parathyroid, airway and oxygenation cues (SpO2 87%, RR 32, hypoxia-induced restlessness) require immediate airway/O2 support first.

questions.prompt: A patient with Cushing's syndrome is experiencing mood changes. What is the nurse's first action?
options: Administer ketoconazole
Check cortisol levels
Encourage exercise
Provide emotional support
questions.rationale: Emotional support helps manage psychological symptoms.

questions.prompt: A 2-year-old child weighing 15 kg is ordered a medication at a dose of 20 mg/kg/day in 3 divided doses. How many milligrams of the medication will the nurse administer per dose?
options: 50 mg
100 mg
200 mg
300 mg
questions.rationale: Correct answer: 100 mg (Verified from PAEDIATRIC QUESTIONS.docx and Saunders 9th Ed.).

questions.prompt: A nurse is caring for several patients on a busy medical-surgical unit. Which of the following patients should the nurse prioritize?
options: A patient with a history of macular degeneration who needs assistance with meal setup
A patient with a hearing aid who needs the batteries changed
A patient with a history of stroke who is experiencing sudden vision changes
A patient with a new prescription for eyeglasses who needs education about care
questions.rationale: Correct answer: A patient with a history of stroke who is experiencing sudden vision changes (Verified from eye and ear  QNS.docx and Saunders 9th Ed.).

questions.prompt: A patient with asthma presents to the emergency department with wheezing and shortness of breath. The nurse notes that the patient's peak expiratory flow rate is 50% of their personal best. What is the nurse's next action?
options: Administer a short-acting beta-agonist
Initiate chest physiotherapy
Increase the patient's oxygen flow rate
Prepare for endotracheal intubation
questions.rationale: A peak expiratory flow rate that is 50% of the patient's personal best indicates a significant decrease in lung function. The nurse should administer a short-acting beta-agonist to promote bronchodilation and improve the patient's breathing.

questions.prompt: A 2-year-old child presents with a "slapped cheek" appearance and a lacy rash on the body. What condition should the nurse suspect?
options: Measles
Roseola
Fifth disease
Scarlet fever
questions.rationale: Correct answer: Fifth disease (Verified from PAEDIATRIC QUESTIONS.docx and Saunders 9th Ed.).

questions.prompt: The nurse notes continuous bubbling in the water seal chamber of a patient's chest tube drainage system. What should the nurse do?
options: Clamp the chest tube
Assess for a leak in the system
Document the finding as normal
Increase the suction
questions.rationale: Continuous bubbling in the water seal chamber indicates a possible air leak in the system. The nurse should assess the chest tube, connections, and drainage system for leaks.

questions.prompt: A nurse is caring for a patient with pneumonia who is receiving supplemental oxygen. What would be the best way to evaluate the effectiveness of the oxygen therapy?
options: Pulse oximetry
Arterial blood gas analysis
Respiratory rate
Blood pressure
questions.rationale: Arterial blood gas analysis provides the most accurate information about the patient's oxygenation status and the effectiveness of oxygen therapy.

questions.prompt: A paediatric nurse is caring for a 6-year-old child who has been prescribed amoxicillin for a bacterial infection. What is the most important instruction to give the child's parents?
options: Give the medication on an empty stomach.
Stop the medication when the child feels better.
Complete the full course of the medication.
Double the dose if the child misses a dose.
questions.rationale: Correct answer: Complete the full course of the medication. (Verified from PAEDIATRIC QUESTIONS.docx and Saunders 9th Ed.).

questions.prompt: The nurse is auscultating a patient's lung sounds and hears a high-pitched, musical sound during expiration. How should the nurse document this finding?
options: Wheezing
Rhonchi
Crackles
Pleural friction rub
questions.rationale: Wheezing is described as a high-pitched, musical sound that is often heard during expiration. It is commonly found in conditions such as asthma or obstructive lung disease.

questions.prompt: A client with glaucoma tells the nurse that she is seeing "halos" around lights. The nurse interprets this as:
options: An expected side effect of the medication
A sign of increased intraocular pressure
A temporary effect that will diminish with time
A result of aging
questions.rationale: Correct answer: A sign of increased intraocular pressure (Verified from eye and ear  QNS.docx and Saunders 9th Ed.).

questions.prompt: A nurse is caring for a patient on mechanical ventilation. The low-pressure alarm sounds. What is the most likely cause?
options: The patient is coughing or has a bronchospasm
The ventilator tubing has become disconnected
The patient is biting on the endotracheal tube
The patient has excessive secretions
questions.rationale: A low-pressure alarm indicates a decrease in airway pressure, which may be caused by a disconnection or leak in the ventilator tubing.

questions.prompt: A patient with acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS) is intubated and receiving mechanical ventilation. The nurse notices a sudden drop in the patient's oxygen saturation. What should the nurse do first?
options: Increase the fraction of inspired oxygen (FiO2) on the ventilator
Check the ventilator tubing for disconnection or kinks
Suction the endotracheal tube
Notify the physician
questions.rationale: The nurse should first check for any mechanical causes of decreased oxygen saturation, such as a disconnection or kinks in the ventilator tubing, which could compromise ventilation.

questions.prompt: A nurse is assessing a 4-year-old child who was recently diagnosed with acute lymphoblastic leukemia (ALL). Which of the following symptoms would the nurse expect to observe?
options: Weight gain and increased appetite
Fatigue and frequent infections
Increased urine output
Rapid breathing and cyanosis
questions.rationale: Correct answer: Fatigue and frequent infections (Verified from PAEDIATRIC QUESTIONS.docx and Saunders 9th Ed.).

questions.prompt: A 12-year-old child with asthma has been prescribed a metered-dose inhaler (MDI). The child is having difficulty coordinating inhalation with medication release. What is the best recommendation the nurse can make?
options: Try using a different type of inhaler.
Use a spacer with the MDI.
Practice more until the child gets it right.
Have a parent administer the medication.
questions.rationale: Correct answer: Use a spacer with the MDI. (Verified from PAEDIATRIC QUESTIONS.docx and Saunders 9th Ed.).

blocks.text: **Anemias, Sickle Cell Crisis, Thrombocytopenia & Blood Transfusions** is a high-yield focus area in **Course Unit 7: Oncology, Hematological Disorders & Oncological Emergencies** for the Next-Generation NCLEX-RN (NGN). This study guide integrates core pathophysiology, clinical judgment cues, pharmacology safety, and bedside nursing priorities across **Saunders Comprehensive Review (9th Ed.)**, **Kaplan NCLEX-RN Prep**, and **LaCharity PDA**.

items: ELITES NURSES FORUM Iron-Defficiency Anemia A. Description 1. Iron stores are depleted, resulting in a decreased iron supply for the manufacture of hemoglobin in red blood cells.
ELITES NURSES FORUM C. Interventions 1. Increase dietary intake of foods rich in vitamin B12, such as meat and liver, if the anemia is a result of a dietary deficiency.

ELITES NURSES FORUM Folate-Deficiency Anemia A. Description 1. A macrocytic anemia in which red blood cells are larger than normal and are oval-shaped rather than round-shaped due to the lack of inadequate intake of folate (vitamin B9).

ELITES NURSES FORUM Aplastic Anemia A. Description 1. Aplastic anemia is a deficiency of circulating erythrocytes and all other formed elements of blood, resulting from the arrested development of cells within the bone marrow.
D. Post transplantation period: Infection, bleeding, or neutropenia and thrombocytopenia are major concerns until engraftment occurs.

ELITES NURSES FORUM Leukemia A malignant progressive disease in which the bone marrow produces increased numbers of immature or abnormal leukocytes. These suppress the production of normal blood cells, leading to anemia and other symptoms.
ELITES NURSES FORUM D. Bleeding 1. During the period of greatest bone marrow suppression (the nadir), the platelet count may be extremely low.

quiz.prompt: A nurse cares for a client presenting with Neutropenia (ANC < 500–1,000) (Anemias, Sickle Cell Crisis, Thrombocytopenia & Blood Transfusions). What is the priority nursing action?
options: Wait 4 hours to reassess before taking any action or documenting.
Administer sedatives or diuretics without reviewing baseline labs or vitals.
Delegate acute clinical assessment and teaching to UAP/CNA.
Even mild fever (>= 100.4°F / 38°C) is a medical emergency!
quiz.rationale: For Neutropenia (ANC < 500–1,000), the priority intervention is: Even mild fever (>= 100.4°F / 38°C) is a medical emergency! Key exam watchpoint: Private room, strict handwashing, NO fresh flowers/raw fruits/rectal temps/enemas.

quiz.prompt: Which statement reflects an unsafe error (or NCLEX trap) that the nurse must AVOID when managing Neutropenia (ANC < 500–1,000)?
options: Private room, strict handwashing, NO fresh flowers/raw fruits/rectal temps/enemas.
Use closed-loop SBAR communication when escalating abnormal clinical changes.
Even mild fever (>= 100.4°F / 38°C) is a medical emergency!
Monitor vital signs, airway, and target labs closely during care of Neutropenia (ANC < 500–1,000).
quiz.rationale: When caring for Neutropenia (ANC < 500–1,000), avoiding this unsafe action is critical: Private room, strict handwashing, NO fresh flowers/raw fruits/rectal temps/enemas.

quiz.prompt: A nurse cares for a client presenting with Thrombocytopenia (Plt < 50k) (Anemias, Sickle Cell Crisis, Thrombocytopenia & Blood Transfusions). What is the priority nursing action?
options: Delegate acute clinical assessment and teaching to UAP/CNA.
Administer sedatives or diuretics without reviewing baseline labs or vitals.
Wait 4 hours to reassess before taking any action or documenting.
Petechiae, ecchymosis, epistaxis, hematuria.
quiz.rationale: For Thrombocytopenia (Plt < 50k), the priority intervention is: Petechiae, ecchymosis, epistaxis, hematuria. Key exam watchpoint: Soft toothbrush, electric razor, avoid IM injections/NSAIDs/straining.

quiz.prompt: A nurse cares for a client presenting with Tumor Lysis Syndrome (TLS) (Anemias, Sickle Cell Crisis, Thrombocytopenia & Blood Transfusions). What is the priority nursing action?
options: Delegate acute clinical assessment and teaching to UAP/CNA.
Administer sedatives or diuretics without reviewing baseline labs or vitals.
High K+, high P+, high Uric Acid, LOW Ca2+ -> AKI.
Wait 4 hours to reassess before taking any action or documenting.
quiz.rationale: For Tumor Lysis Syndrome (TLS), the priority intervention is: High K+, high P+, high Uric Acid, LOW Ca2+ -> AKI. Key exam watchpoint: Aggressive IV hydration + Allopurinol / Rasburicase + cardiac monitoring.

quiz.prompt: A nurse cares for a client presenting with Brachytherapy (Internal Rad) (Anemias, Sickle Cell Crisis, Thrombocytopenia & Blood Transfusions). What is the priority nursing action?
options: Sealed radioactive implant inside client.
Administer sedatives or diuretics without reviewing baseline labs or vitals.
Wait 4 hours to reassess before taking any action or documenting.
Delegate acute clinical assessment and teaching to UAP/CNA.
quiz.rationale: For Brachytherapy (Internal Rad), the priority intervention is: Sealed radioactive implant inside client. Key exam watchpoint: Private room, lead shield, 30-min/shift limit, long forceps + lead container for dislodged implant.

quiz.prompt: A client managed for Anemias, Sickle Cell Crisis, Thrombocytopenia & Blood Transfusions develops sudden tachypnea (RR 32/min), SpO2 87%, and new-onset restlessness. What should the nurse do FIRST?
options: Elevate the head of the bed, assess airway/lung sounds, and apply supplemental oxygen.
Ask the UAP to assist the client to ambulate in the hallway.
Document the vital signs and recheck oxygen saturation in 2 hours.
Administer a PRN opioid analgesic for restlessness before assessing.
quiz.rationale: Under Maslow's hierarchy and ABC prioritization in Anemias, Sickle Cell Crisis, Thrombocytopenia & Blood Transfusions, airway and oxygenation cues (SpO2 87%, RR 32, hypoxia-induced restlessness) require immediate airway/O2 support first.

quiz.prompt: Which client care task related to Anemias, Sickle Cell Crisis, Thrombocytopenia & Blood Transfusions is appropriate to delegate to an Unlicensed Assistive Personnel (UAP)?
options: Performing the comprehensive admission assessment for a newly arrived acute client.
Providing initial discharge teaching on red-flag warning signs.
Obtaining routine vital signs and strictly measuring oral intake and urine output on a stable client.
Evaluating the client's therapeutic response to an intravenous high-alert medication.
quiz.rationale: Per LaCharity PDA and NCSBN delegation rules, UAPs perform routine, stable data collection (vitals, I&O, ADLs), while assessment, teaching, and evaluation remain RN-only duties.

quiz.prompt: A preceptor reviews discharge teaching for a client recovering under Anemias, Sickle Cell Crisis, Thrombocytopenia & Blood Transfusions. Which statement by the client indicates teaching was effective?
options: "I will monitor for warning signs like fever, worsening shortness of breath, or bleeding and contact my provider promptly."
"I do not need follow-up lab monitoring because my hospital discharge labs were normal."
"It is fine to take over-the-counter NSAIDs alongside my prescribed anticoagulants without asking."
"Once I feel a little better tomorrow, I can stop taking all prescribed medications."
quiz.rationale: Effective client education in Anemias, Sickle Cell Crisis, Thrombocytopenia & Blood Transfusions requires adherence to therapy, scheduled lab follow-ups, and prompt reporting of acute deterioration.

quiz.prompt: When using the NCSBN 6-Step Clinical Judgment Model (CJMM) for a client in Course Unit 7: Oncology, Hematological Disorders & Oncological Emergencies, what directly follows 'Recognize Cues' and 'Analyze Cues'?
options: Archive the admission chart without creating a care plan.
Delegate hypothesis ranking to support staff before completing assessment.
Prioritize Hypotheses — ranking immediate life-threatening complications first.
Evaluate Outcomes prior to implementing any bedside intervention.
quiz.rationale: The 6 steps of the NCSBN CJMM progress in order: Recognize Cues -> Analyze Cues -> Prioritize Hypotheses -> Generate Solutions -> Take Action -> Evaluate Outcomes.

quiz.prompt: A patient is experiencing vertigo. The nurse knows that this symptom is likely related to a problem with what part of the sensory system?
options: Visual system
Vestibular system
Olfactory system
Tactile system
quiz.rationale: The vestibular system (B), located within the inner ear, is responsible for maintaining balance and spatial orientation. Vertigo, a sensation of feeling off balance, is often caused by problems in this system. The visual (A), olfactory (C), and tactile (D) systems are not typically associated with symptoms of vertigo.

quiz.prompt: As a nurse leader, you notice that one of your team members is consistently late for their shift. What is the most appropriate action?
options: Ignore the behavior as it doesn't affect patient care.
Report the behavior to the hospital administration.
Discuss the issue with the team member privately.
Publicly reprimand the team member during a staff meeting.
quiz.rationale: In this situation, the most appropriate action for a nurse leader is to address the issue directly with the individual involved (C). Ignoring the behavior (A) is not an effective leadership strategy as it fails to address the issue. Reporting the behavior to administration (B) should be a last resort if the behavior continues after addressing it directly. Publicly reprimanding the team member (D) is not appropriate and could create a hostile work environment.

quiz.prompt: As a nurse leader, you are implementing a change in a hospital protocol. What is the best way to ensure staff compliance with this change?
options: Enforce strict punishments for non-compliance.
Communicate the rationale for the change.
Make the change without explaining why.
Implement the change without seeking staff input.
quiz.rationale: Effective leadership involves open and clear communication. Explaining the rationale for the change (B) helps staff understand the importance and necessity of the change, thereby fostering compliance. Enforcing strict punishments (A) tends to create a negative work environment. Implementing a change without explanation (C) or without seeking staff input (D) can lead to resistance and non-compliance.

quiz.prompt: A nurse is teaching a patient who has been diagnosed with glaucoma. Which of the following statements by the patient indicates the need for further teaching?
options: "I will need to use my eye drops daily."
"I will avoid straining during bowel movements."
"I am glad I can stop taking my eye drops once my symptoms improve."
"I understand that I will need regular check-ups for my eye pressure."
quiz.rationale: Correct answer: "I am glad I can stop taking my eye drops once my symptoms improve." (Verified from eye and ear  QNS.docx and Saunders 9th Ed.).

quiz.prompt: A nurse is providing leadership training to a group of new graduate nurses. Which of the following leadership styles is likely to be most effective for promoting autonomy and critical thinking among the new nurses?
options: Autocratic
Laissez-faire
Democratic
Transactional
quiz.rationale: Correct answer: Democratic (Verified from eye and ear  QNS.docx and Saunders 9th Ed.).

quiz.prompt: A nurse is assessing a patient with suspected macular degeneration. Which of the following findings would most likely indicate this condition?
options: Loss of peripheral vision
Difficulty distinguishing colors
Blurred vision
Central vision loss
quiz.rationale: Correct answer: Central vision loss (Verified from eye and ear  QNS.docx and Saunders 9th Ed.).

quiz.prompt: As a nurse leader, you observe a conflict between two team members. What is the most appropriate initial action?
options: Ignore the conflict and hope it resolves itself.
Immediately report the incident to higher management.
Facilitate a meeting between the two individuals to discuss the issue.
Take sides with the person who has been with the team longer.
quiz.rationale: Correct answer: Facilitate a meeting between the two individuals to discuss the issue. (Verified from eye and ear  QNS.docx and Saunders 9th Ed.).

quiz.prompt: A patient with diabetes reports experiencing numbness and tingling in their feet. This is most likely indicative of which of the following conditions?
options: Diabetic retinopathy
Diabetic neuropathy
Diabetic nephropathy
Diabetic ketoacidosis
quiz.rationale: Correct answer: Diabetic neuropathy (Verified from eye and ear  QNS.docx and Saunders 9th Ed.).

quiz.prompt: A patient with a history of glaucoma has been prescribed eye drops to decrease intraocular pressure. The patient also has other chronic conditions that require medication. Which of the following should be the nurse's priority instruction?
options: "Take your glaucoma eye drops first before any other medication."
"You can take your glaucoma eye drops at the same time as your other medications."
"Take your glaucoma eye drops last after all other medications."
"The timing of your glaucoma eye drops in relation to other medications doesn't matter."
quiz.rationale: Correct answer: "Take your glaucoma eye drops first before any other medication." (Verified from eye and ear  QNS.docx and Saunders 9th Ed.).

quiz.prompt: A nurse is prioritizing care for a patient who has been newly diagnosed with Meniere's disease. Which of the following should be the nurse's first action?
options: Providing patient education about the disease
Starting the patient on a low-sodium diet
Administering prescribed medication
Assessing the patient's current level of knowledge
quiz.rationale: Correct answer: Assessing the patient's current level of knowledge (Verified from eye and ear  QNS.docx and Saunders 9th Ed.).

quiz.prompt: A patient with a spinal cord injury report experiencing phantom limb pain. The nurse should prioritize which of the following interventions?
options: Administering prescribed pain medication
Reassuring the patient that the pain is not real
Teaching the patient distraction techniques
Assessing the patient's pain level and characteristics
quiz.rationale: Correct answer: Assessing the patient's pain level and characteristics (Verified from eye and ear  QNS.docx and Saunders 9th Ed.).

items: ELITES NURSES FORUM E. Superior vena cava syndrome Description a. Superior vena cava (SVC) syndrome occurs when the SVC is compressed or obstructed by tumor growth (commonly associated with lung cancer and lymphoma).
ELITES NURSES FORUM Superior Vena Cava Syndrome ELITES NURSES FORUM 2. Interventions a. Assess for early signs and symptoms of SVC syndrome.
ELITES NURSES FORUM Chemotherapy Causes immunosuppression ○ Destroys cancer cells ○ Stops cancer cell growth ○ Prevents cancer cells from metastasizing But….this destroys healthy cells too.
ELITES NURSES FORUM V. Chemotherapy A. Description 1. Chemotherapy kills or inhibits the reproduction of neoplastic cells and kills normal cells.

ELITES NURSES FORUM VI. Radiation Therapy A. Description 1. Radiation therapy destroys cancer cells, with minimal exposure of normal cells to the damaging effects of radiation. The damaged cells die or become unable to divide.
B. External beam radiation (teletherapy): The actual radiation source is external to the client.
ELITES NURSES FORUM External Radiation Precautions ELITES NURSES FORUM C. Brachytherapy 1. The radiation source comes into direct, continuous contact with tumor tissues for a specific time.
ELITES NURSES FORUM ELITES NURSES FORUM 7. Unsealed radiation source a. Administration is via the oral or IV route or by instillation into body cavities.

ELITES NURSES FORUM 8. Sealed radiation source (see Clinical Judgment: Take Action Box) (Box 45.6) a. A sealed, temporary or permanent radiation source (solid implant) is implanted within the tumor target tissues.
ELITES NURSES FORUM 9. Removal of sealed radiation sources a. The client is not radioactive after removal.

items: ELITES NURSES FORUM E. Superior vena cava syndrome Description a. Superior vena cava (SVC) syndrome occurs when the SVC is compressed or obstructed by tumor growth (commonly associated with lung cancer and lymphoma).
ELITES NURSES FORUM B. Metastasis 1. Cancer cells move from their original location to other sites.
B. Biopsy 1. Description a. Biopsy is the definitive means of diagnosing cancer and provides histological proof of malignancy.
IV. Surgery A. Description: Surgery is indicated to diagnose, stage, and treat certain types of cancer.

B. Prophylactic surgery 1. Prophylactic surgery is performed in clients with an existing premalignant condition or a known family history or genetic mutation that strongly predisposes the person to the development of cancer.
D. Control (cytoreductive or “debulking”) surgery 1. Control surgery is a debulking procedure that consists of removing a large portion of a locally invasive tumor, such as advanced ovarian cancer.

ELITES NURSES FORUM CONT F. Reconstructive or rehabilitative surgery is performed to improve quality of life by restoring maximal function and appearance, such as breast reconstruction after mastectomy.
ELITES NURSES FORUM Chemotherapy Causes immunosuppression ○ Destroys cancer cells ○ Stops cancer cell growth ○ Prevents cancer cells from metastasizing But….this destroys healthy cells too.

ELITES NURSES FORUM VI. Radiation Therapy A. Description 1. Radiation therapy destroys cancer cells, with minimal exposure of normal cells to the damaging effects of radiation. The damaged cells die or become unable to divide.
ELITES NURSES FORUM Symptoms Painless lump in the breast or underarm Flattening or indentation on the breast.
