questions.rationale: Correct answer: Assessing the patient's pain level and characteristics (Verified from eye and ear  QNS.docx and Saunders 9th Ed.).

questions.prompt: A nurse is providing leadership training to a group of new graduate nurses. Which of the following leadership styles is likely to be most effective for promoting autonomy and critical thinking among the new nurses?
options: Autocratic
Laissez-faire
Democratic
Transactional
questions.rationale: Correct answer: Democratic (Verified from eye and ear  QNS.docx and Saunders 9th Ed.).

questions.prompt: A preceptor reviews discharge teaching for a client recovering under Breast, Lung, Colorectal, Prostate & Cervical Cancers (CAUTION). Which statement by the client indicates teaching was effective?
options: "Once I feel a little better tomorrow, I can stop taking all prescribed medications."
"I will monitor for warning signs like fever, worsening shortness of breath, or bleeding and contact my provider promptly."
"It is fine to take over-the-counter NSAIDs alongside my prescribed anticoagulants without asking."
"I do not need follow-up lab monitoring because my hospital discharge labs were normal."
questions.rationale: Effective client education in Breast, Lung, Colorectal, Prostate & Cervical Cancers (CAUTION) requires adherence to therapy, scheduled lab follow-ups, and prompt reporting of acute deterioration.

questions.prompt: As a nurse leader, you observe a conflict between two team members. What is the most appropriate initial action?
options: Ignore the conflict and hope it resolves itself.
Immediately report the incident to higher management.
Facilitate a meeting between the two individuals to discuss the issue.
Take sides with the person who has been with the team longer.
questions.rationale: Correct answer: Facilitate a meeting between the two individuals to discuss the issue. (Verified from eye and ear  QNS.docx and Saunders 9th Ed.).

questions.prompt: A nurse is teaching a patient who has been diagnosed with glaucoma. Which of the following statements by the patient indicates the need for further teaching?
options: "I will need to use my eye drops daily."
"I will avoid straining during bowel movements."
"I am glad I can stop taking my eye drops once my symptoms improve."
"I understand that I will need regular check-ups for my eye pressure."
questions.rationale: Correct answer: "I am glad I can stop taking my eye drops once my symptoms improve." (Verified from eye and ear  QNS.docx and Saunders 9th Ed.).

questions.prompt: As a nurse leader, you notice that one of your team members is consistently late for their shift. What is the most appropriate action?
options: Ignore the behavior as it doesn't affect patient care.
Report the behavior to the hospital administration.
Discuss the issue with the team member privately.
Publicly reprimand the team member during a staff meeting.
questions.rationale: In this situation, the most appropriate action for a nurse leader is to address the issue directly with the individual involved (C). Ignoring the behavior (A) is not an effective leadership strategy as it fails to address the issue. Reporting the behavior to administration (B) should be a last resort if the behavior continues after addressing it directly. Publicly reprimanding the team member (D) is not appropriate and could create a hostile work environment.

questions.prompt: A nurse is assessing a patient with suspected macular degeneration. Which of the following findings would most likely indicate this condition?
options: Loss of peripheral vision
Difficulty distinguishing colors
Blurred vision
Central vision loss
questions.rationale: Correct answer: Central vision loss (Verified from eye and ear  QNS.docx and Saunders 9th Ed.).

questions.prompt: Which statement reflects an unsafe error (or NCLEX trap) that the nurse must AVOID when managing Neutropenia (ANC < 500–1,000)?
options: Even mild fever (>= 100.4°F / 38°C) is a medical emergency!
Use closed-loop SBAR communication when escalating abnormal clinical changes.
Private room, strict handwashing, NO fresh flowers/raw fruits/rectal temps/enemas.
Monitor vital signs, airway, and target labs closely during care of Neutropenia (ANC < 500–1,000).
questions.rationale: When caring for Neutropenia (ANC < 500–1,000), avoiding this unsafe action is critical: Private room, strict handwashing, NO fresh flowers/raw fruits/rectal temps/enemas.

questions.prompt: A nurse cares for a client presenting with Thrombocytopenia (Plt < 50k) (Breast, Lung, Colorectal, Prostate & Cervical Cancers (CAUTION)). What is the priority nursing action?
options: Petechiae, ecchymosis, epistaxis, hematuria.
Wait 4 hours to reassess before taking any action or documenting.
Administer sedatives or diuretics without reviewing baseline labs or vitals.
Delegate acute clinical assessment and teaching to UAP/CNA.
questions.rationale: For Thrombocytopenia (Plt < 50k), the priority intervention is: Petechiae, ecchymosis, epistaxis, hematuria. Key exam watchpoint: Soft toothbrush, electric razor, avoid IM injections/NSAIDs/straining.

questions.prompt: As a nurse leader, you are implementing a change in a hospital protocol. What is the best way to ensure staff compliance with this change?
options: Enforce strict punishments for non-compliance.
Communicate the rationale for the change.
Make the change without explaining why.
Implement the change without seeking staff input.
questions.rationale: Effective leadership involves open and clear communication. Explaining the rationale for the change (B) helps staff understand the importance and necessity of the change, thereby fostering compliance. Enforcing strict punishments (A) tends to create a negative work environment. Implementing a change without explanation (C) or without seeking staff input (D) can lead to resistance and non-compliance.

questions.prompt: A patient with diabetes reports experiencing numbness and tingling in their feet. This is most likely indicative of which of the following conditions?
options: Diabetic retinopathy
Diabetic neuropathy
Diabetic nephropathy
Diabetic ketoacidosis
questions.rationale: Correct answer: Diabetic neuropathy (Verified from eye and ear  QNS.docx and Saunders 9th Ed.).

questions.prompt: Which client care task related to Anemias, Sickle Cell Crisis, Thrombocytopenia & Blood Transfusions is appropriate to delegate to an Unlicensed Assistive Personnel (UAP)?
options: Performing the comprehensive admission assessment for a newly arrived acute client.
Providing initial discharge teaching on red-flag warning signs.
Obtaining routine vital signs and strictly measuring oral intake and urine output on a stable client.
Evaluating the client's therapeutic response to an intravenous high-alert medication.
questions.rationale: Per LaCharity PDA and NCSBN delegation rules, UAPs perform routine, stable data collection (vitals, I&O, ADLs), while assessment, teaching, and evaluation remain RN-only duties.

questions.prompt: A client managed for Anemias, Sickle Cell Crisis, Thrombocytopenia & Blood Transfusions develops sudden tachypnea (RR 32/min), SpO2 87%, and new-onset restlessness. What should the nurse do FIRST?
options: Elevate the head of the bed, assess airway/lung sounds, and apply supplemental oxygen.
Ask the UAP to assist the client to ambulate in the hallway.
Document the vital signs and recheck oxygen saturation in 2 hours.
Administer a PRN opioid analgesic for restlessness before assessing.
questions.rationale: Under Maslow's hierarchy and ABC prioritization in Anemias, Sickle Cell Crisis, Thrombocytopenia & Blood Transfusions, airway and oxygenation cues (SpO2 87%, RR 32, hypoxia-induced restlessness) require immediate airway/O2 support first.

questions.prompt: A preceptor reviews discharge teaching for a client recovering under Anemias, Sickle Cell Crisis, Thrombocytopenia & Blood Transfusions. Which statement by the client indicates teaching was effective?
options: "I will monitor for warning signs like fever, worsening shortness of breath, or bleeding and contact my provider promptly."
"I do not need follow-up lab monitoring because my hospital discharge labs were normal."
"It is fine to take over-the-counter NSAIDs alongside my prescribed anticoagulants without asking."
"Once I feel a little better tomorrow, I can stop taking all prescribed medications."
questions.rationale: Effective client education in Anemias, Sickle Cell Crisis, Thrombocytopenia & Blood Transfusions requires adherence to therapy, scheduled lab follow-ups, and prompt reporting of acute deterioration.

questions.prompt: A nurse cares for a client presenting with Brachytherapy (Internal Rad) (Oncological Emergencies (TLS, SIADH, SVC, Hypercalcemia) & Chemo). What is the priority nursing action?
options: Delegate acute clinical assessment and teaching to UAP/CNA.
Administer sedatives or diuretics without reviewing baseline labs or vitals.
Sealed radioactive implant inside client.
Wait 4 hours to reassess before taking any action or documenting.
questions.rationale: For Brachytherapy (Internal Rad), the priority intervention is: Sealed radioactive implant inside client. Key exam watchpoint: Private room, lead shield, 30-min/shift limit, long forceps + lead container for dislodged implant.

questions.prompt: A client managed for Oncological Emergencies (TLS, SIADH, SVC, Hypercalcemia) & Chemo develops sudden tachypnea (RR 32/min), SpO2 87%, and new-onset restlessness. What should the nurse do FIRST?
options: Document the vital signs and recheck oxygen saturation in 2 hours.
Ask the UAP to assist the client to ambulate in the hallway.
Administer a PRN opioid analgesic for restlessness before assessing.
Elevate the head of the bed, assess airway/lung sounds, and apply supplemental oxygen.
questions.rationale: Under Maslow's hierarchy and ABC prioritization in Oncological Emergencies (TLS, SIADH, SVC, Hypercalcemia) & Chemo, airway and oxygenation cues (SpO2 87%, RR 32, hypoxia-induced restlessness) require immediate airway/O2 support first.

questions.prompt: A client managed for Breast, Lung, Colorectal, Prostate & Cervical Cancers (CAUTION) develops sudden tachypnea (RR 32/min), SpO2 87%, and new-onset restlessness. What should the nurse do FIRST?
options: Administer a PRN opioid analgesic for restlessness before assessing.
Document the vital signs and recheck oxygen saturation in 2 hours.
Elevate the head of the bed, assess airway/lung sounds, and apply supplemental oxygen.
Ask the UAP to assist the client to ambulate in the hallway.
questions.rationale: Under Maslow's hierarchy and ABC prioritization in Breast, Lung, Colorectal, Prostate & Cervical Cancers (CAUTION), airway and oxygenation cues (SpO2 87%, RR 32, hypoxia-induced restlessness) require immediate airway/O2 support first.

questions.prompt: Which client care task related to Oncological Emergencies (TLS, SIADH, SVC, Hypercalcemia) & Chemo is appropriate to delegate to an Unlicensed Assistive Personnel (UAP)?
options: Obtaining routine vital signs and strictly measuring oral intake and urine output on a stable client.
Providing initial discharge teaching on red-flag warning signs.
Performing the comprehensive admission assessment for a newly arrived acute client.
Evaluating the client's therapeutic response to an intravenous high-alert medication.
questions.rationale: Per LaCharity PDA and NCSBN delegation rules, UAPs perform routine, stable data collection (vitals, I&O, ADLs), while assessment, teaching, and evaluation remain RN-only duties.

questions.prompt: A paediatric nurse is caring for a 6-year-old child who has been prescribed amoxicillin for a bacterial infection. What is the most important instruction to give the child's parents?
options: Give the medication on an empty stomach.
Stop the medication when the child feels better.
Complete the full course of the medication.
Double the dose if the child misses a dose.
questions.rationale: Correct answer: Complete the full course of the medication. (Verified from PAEDIATRIC QUESTIONS.docx and Saunders 9th Ed.).

questions.prompt: A patient with type 2 diabetes is taking metformin. What is the primary goal of treatment?
options: Increase insulin production
Decrease glucose production
Increase insulin sensitivity
Decrease glucose absorption
questions.rationale: Metformin works by increasing insulin sensitivity, reducing glucose production in the liver, and enhancing glucose uptake in muscles.

questions.prompt: A child with osteosarcoma reports pain in the affected leg. The nurse has delegated the administration of oral pain medication to a nursing assistant. What is the most appropriate action by the nurse?
options: The nurse should administer the medication instead
The nurse should assess the child's pain before and after medication administration
The nurse should instruct the nursing assistant to assess the child's pain level
The nurse should document the administration of the medication
questions.rationale: The nurse cannot delegate the administration of medication or the assessment of pain to a nursing assistant. These tasks fall within the nurse's scope of practice. The nurse should assess the child's pain before and after medication administration to determine the effectiveness of the medication.

questions.prompt: A nurse is caring for a patient on mechanical ventilation. The low-pressure alarm sounds. What is the most likely cause?
options: The patient is coughing or has a bronchospasm
The ventilator tubing has become disconnected
The patient is biting on the endotracheal tube
The patient has excessive secretions
questions.rationale: A low-pressure alarm indicates a decrease in airway pressure, which may be caused by a disconnection or leak in the ventilator tubing.

questions.prompt: A nurse is caring for a client who has a tracheostomy. Which of the following interventions should the nurse include in the plan of care?
options: Provide tracheostomy care every shift
Use sterile technique when suctioning the tracheostomy
Encourage the client to cough and deep breathe every 2 hours
All of the above
questions.rationale: All the listed interventions are part of the appropriate care for a client with a tracheostomy. They all help maintain a patent airway, promote effective gas exchange, and prevent infection.

questions.prompt: Question: A 2-year-old patient is suspected of having iron-deficiency anemia. Which symptom is most likely to be observed?
options: Frequent nosebleeds
Unexplained bruises
Rapid heart rate
Yellowing of the skin and eyes
questions.rationale: Correct answer: Rapid heart rate (Verified from PAEDIATRIC QUESTIONS.docx and Saunders 9th Ed.).

questions.prompt: A patient with type 2 diabetes is taking pioglitazone. What is the primary goal of treatment?
options: Increase insulin production
Decrease glucose production
Increase insulin sensitivity
Decrease glucose absorption
questions.rationale: Pioglitazone enhances insulin sensitivity, improving glucose uptake.

questions.prompt: A nurse is assessing a patient with a suspected diagnosis of Meniere's disease. Which of the following symptoms would the nurse expect to find?
options: Tinnitus
Dry eyes
Double vision
Loss of taste
questions.rationale: Correct answer: Tinnitus (Verified from eye and ear  QNS.docx and Saunders 9th Ed.).

questions.prompt: A nurse is providing dietary education to the parents of a child with celiac disease. Which food should the nurse instruct the parents to eliminate from the child's diet?
options: Rice
Wheat
Corn
Potatoes
questions.rationale: Celiac disease is a disorder where ingestion of gluten leads to damage in the small intestine. Gluten is found in wheat, rye, and barley. Therefore, wheat should be eliminated from the diet of a child with celiac disease. Rice (option A), corn (option C), and potatoes (option D) are naturally gluten-free and can be included in the diet.

questions.prompt: A patient who underwent a myringotomy report experiencing pain in the ear. What should the nurse's initial response be?
options: Administer prescribed pain medication
Report the pain to the healthcare provider
Reassure the patient that pain is normal after this procedure
Check the patient's ear for signs of infection
questions.rationale: While some discomfort might be expected after a myringotomy, severe or increasing pain could indicate a complication such as infection. Therefore, the nurse should first check the patient's ear for signs of infection, such as redness, swelling, and discharge. Option A could be appropriate after the nurse has assessed the patient and ruled out complications. Option B might be appropriate if signs of infection are found. Option C is incorrect because it could delay treatment of a potential complication.

questions.prompt: A 2-year-old child has been diagnosed with lead poisoning. Which of the following symptoms would the nurse expect to observe?
options: Hyperactivity and impulsivity
Weight gain and increased appetite
Increased urine output
Developmental delays and irritability
questions.rationale: Correct answer: Developmental delays and irritability (Verified from PAEDIATRIC QUESTIONS.docx and Saunders 9th Ed.).

questions.prompt: A 6-year-old child weighing 20 kg is scheduled to receive a dose of medication. The medication is ordered at a dose of 5 mg/kg/dose every 8 hours. The medication comes in a concentration of 100 mg/5 mL. How many milliliters of medication will the nurse administer per dose?
options: 1 mL
2 mL
3 mL
5 mL
questions.rationale: Correct answer: 2 mL (Verified from PAEDIATRIC QUESTIONS.docx and Saunders 9th Ed.).

questions.prompt: A nurse is assessing a 4-year-old child who was recently diagnosed with acute lymphoblastic leukemia (ALL). Which of the following symptoms would the nurse expect to observe?
options: Weight gain and increased appetite
Fatigue and frequent infections
Increased urine output
Rapid breathing and cyanosis
questions.rationale: Correct answer: Fatigue and frequent infections (Verified from PAEDIATRIC QUESTIONS.docx and Saunders 9th Ed.).

questions.prompt: A nurse is caring for a patient who has a tracheostomy. Which of the following interventions would the nurse include in the plan of care to prevent a common complication associated with a tracheostomy?
options: Frequent oral care
Encourage ambulation
Turn the patient every 2 hours
Provide a high protein diet
questions.rationale: Frequent oral care helps to prevent infections, a common complication associated with a tracheostomy.

questions.prompt: A patient with chronic bronchitis has poor appetite and has lost weight. What dietary modification should the nurse suggest?
options: Low-fat diet
High-protein, high-calorie diet
Low-sodium diet
Low-carbohydrate diet
questions.rationale: Patients with chronic bronchitis often have difficulty eating and may lose weight. A high-protein, high-calorie diet can help to maintain their nutritional status and support their immune function.

questions.prompt: A patient with Cushing's syndrome is experiencing weight gain and hypertension. What is the nurse's first action?
options: Administer ketoconazole
Check cortisol levels
Encourage exercise
Provide emotional support
questions.rationale: Ketoconazole helps decrease cortisol production.

questions.prompt: A nurse is assessing a 6-month-old infant with pyloric stenosis. Which symptom is most characteristic of this condition?
options: Projectile vomiting
Severe diarrhea
Frequent loose stools
Abdominal distension
questions.rationale: Pyloric stenosis is a condition where the opening from the stomach into the small intestine (the pylorus) has thickened and narrowed, obstructing food passage. This often results in projectile vomiting after feeding. Severe diarrhea (option B), frequent loose stools (option C), and abdominal distension (option D) are not typically associated with pyloric stenosis.

questions.prompt: A nurse is caring for a patient who is 2 days post-op from a thoracotomy. The patient is reluctant to perform deep breathing exercises due to pain. Which of the following interventions should the nurse implement?
options: Administer pain medication before the exercises
Encourage shallow breathing to prevent discomfort
Discontinue the exercises until the pain subsides
Encourage the patient to hold their breath as long as possible
questions.rationale: Deep breathing exercises are critical after thoracotomy to prevent complications such as pneumonia and atelectasis. Administering pain medication before the exercises can help alleviate the patient's discomfort and encourage compliance.

questions.prompt: A nurse is caring for a client with a hearing impairment. Which of the following interventions should the nurse implement to promote effective communication?
options: Speak loudly and over-enunciate each word
Maintain direct eye contact and speak in a normal tone
Speak to the client from behind to reduce distractions
Use complex medical terminologies to explain the condition
questions.rationale: Correct answer: Maintain direct eye contact and speak in a normal tone (Verified from eye and ear  QNS.docx and Saunders 9th Ed.).

questions.prompt: The nurse is caring for a child with Hirschsprung disease. Which of the following symptoms is most common in this condition?
options: Diarrhea
Constipation
Vomiting
Abdominal pain
questions.rationale: Hirschsprung disease is a congenital condition characterized by the absence of nerve cells in part of the intestine, resulting in chronic constipation. Diarrhea (option A), vomiting (option C), and abdominal pain (option D) can occur but are not as common.

questions.prompt: A 2-year-old child presents with a "slapped cheek" appearance and a lacy rash on the body. What condition should the nurse suspect?
options: Measles
Roseola
Fifth disease
Scarlet fever
questions.rationale: Correct answer: Fifth disease (Verified from PAEDIATRIC QUESTIONS.docx and Saunders 9th Ed.).

questions.prompt: A 7-year-old child is newly diagnosed with Type 1 Diabetes Mellitus. The nurse would expect which of the following symptoms to have been present before diagnosis?
options: Weight gain
Bradycardia
Polydipsia
Hypertension
questions.rationale: Polydipsia (excessive thirst) is a classic symptom of Type 1 Diabetes Mellitus due to the body's inability to properly handle glucose, leading to high blood sugar levels and dehydration. Weight gain (option A) is more commonly associated with Type 2 Diabetes. Bradycardia (option B) and hypertension (option D) are not typical symptoms of Type 1 Diabetes.

questions.prompt: A nurse is caring for a 6-year-old child who was recently diagnosed with asthma. Which of the following should the nurse include in the child's asthma action plan?
options: Teach the child to recognize and avoid triggers
Instruct the child to use a short-acting bronchodilator daily
Encourage the child to participate in sports without restrictions
Advise the child to decrease fluid intake to reduce mucus production
questions.rationale: Correct answer: Teach the child to recognize and avoid triggers (Verified from PAEDIATRIC QUESTIONS.docx and Saunders 9th Ed.).

questions.prompt: A patient presents to the emergency department with sudden onset of sharp, severe chest pain and shortness of breath. The patient's blood pressure is 90/60 mmHg, heart rate is 120 beats per minute, and oxygen saturation is 90%. What should the nurse suspect?
options: Myocardial infarction
Pneumonia
Pulmonary embolism
Asthma attack
questions.rationale: The patient's symptoms of sudden onset of severe chest pain, shortness of breath, tachycardia, hypotension, and low oxygen saturation are indicative of a pulmonary embolism, a life-threatening emergency.

questions.prompt: A patient with tuberculosis is started on a regimen of multiple antibiotics. What should the nurse include in patient teaching regarding this treatment?
options: The patient will need to be on antibiotics for several weeks
The patient should expect a rapid improvement in symptoms
The patient should not drink alcohol while on these medications
All of the above
questions.rationale: Tuberculosis requires a prolonged treatment with multiple antibiotics, often for several months. The patient should be cautioned not to drink alcohol while on these medications due to potential for liver damage. It's also important to inform the patient that although they might feel better, they need to finish the full course of antibiotics to fully treat the infection.

questions.prompt: The nurse notes continuous bubbling in the water seal chamber of a patient's chest tube drainage system. What should the nurse do?
options: Clamp the chest tube
Assess for a leak in the system
Document the finding as normal
Increase the suction
questions.rationale: Continuous bubbling in the water seal chamber indicates a possible air leak in the system. The nurse should assess the chest tube, connections, and drainage system for leaks.

questions.prompt: A 15-year-old child with Type 1 Diabetes Mellitus is admitted to the hospital for diabetic ketoacidosis (DKA). Which of the following would the nurse expect to observe?
options: Hypoglycemia
Bradycardia
Kussmaul respirations
Decreased urine output
questions.rationale: Kussmaul respirations (rapid, deep breathing) are a common symptom of DKA, as the body tries to compensate for metabolic acidosis by blowing off excess carbon dioxide. Hypoglycemia (option A) is not typically associated with DKA; instead, blood glucose levels are usually high. Bradycardia (option B) and decreased urine output (option D) are not typical symptoms of DKA.

questions.prompt: A nurse is caring for a patient with asthma. Which of the following assessments would indicate an impending asthma attack?
options: Decreased wheezing
Increased peak flow rate
Sudden restlessness and anxiety
Decreased pulse rate
questions.rationale: A sudden change in behaviour, such as increased restlessness and anxiety, can indicate hypoxia, which could be a sign of an impending asthma attack.

questions.prompt: The charge nurse is delegating tasks for the day. Which of the following tasks can be delegated to a nursing assistant?
options: Administering medications
Performing sterile dressing changes
Assessing a patient's pain level
Assisting a patient with personal hygiene
questions.rationale: Correct answer: Assisting a patient with personal hygiene (Verified from eye and ear  QNS.docx and Saunders 9th Ed.).

questions.prompt: A nurse is caring for a client with tuberculosis. Which of the following actions should the nurse take to prevent the spread of the disease?
options: Wear a mask when providing direct patient care
Place the patient in a private room
Wash hands after removing gloves
All of the above
questions.rationale: Tuberculosis is an airborne disease. It is crucial to wear a mask, place the patient in a private room, and wash hands after removing gloves to prevent the spread of the disease.

questions.prompt: A 5-year-old child is admitted with suspected appendicitis. Which symptom is the nurse likely to find?
options: Diarrhea
Right lower quadrant pain
Left upper quadrant pain
Constipation
questions.rationale: The most common symptom of appendicitis is abdominal pain that begins near the belly button and then shifts to the lower right side of the abdomen. Diarrhea (option A) and constipation (option D) can occur but are not as specific. Left upper quadrant pain (option C) is not typically associated with appendicitis.

questions.prompt: The nurse is providing discharge teaching for the parents of an infant with gastroesophageal reflux disease (GERD). Which instruction should be included?
options: Feed the infant larger, less frequent meals
Position the infant flat after feeding
Thicken the infant's formula with rice cereal
Change the formula to a cow's milk-based formula
questions.rationale: Correct answer: Thicken the infant's formula with rice cereal (Verified from PAEDIATRIC QUESTIONS.docx and Saunders 9th Ed.).

questions.prompt: A patient with hyperparathyroidism is taking calcitonin. What is the primary goal of treatment?
options: Decrease calcium levels
Increase calcium levels
Regulate bone metabolism
Reduce kidney stone formation
questions.rationale: Calcitonin helps lower calcium levels by inhibiting osteoclast activity.

questions.prompt: A nurse is caring for several patients on a busy medical-surgical unit. Which of the following patients should the nurse prioritize?
options: A patient with a history of macular degeneration who needs assistance with meal setup
A patient with a hearing aid who needs the batteries changed
A patient with a history of stroke who is experiencing sudden vision changes
A patient with a new prescription for eyeglasses who needs education about care
questions.rationale: Correct answer: A patient with a history of stroke who is experiencing sudden vision changes (Verified from eye and ear  QNS.docx and Saunders 9th Ed.).

blocks.text: **Types I–IV Hypersensitivity, Anaphylaxis & Latex Allergy Precautions** is a high-yield focus area in **Course Unit 8: Immune System, Hypersensitivity, HIV/AIDS & Autoimmune Care** for the Next-Generation NCLEX-RN (NGN). This study guide integrates core pathophysiology, clinical judgment cues, pharmacology safety, and bedside nursing priorities across **Saunders Comprehensive Review (9th Ed.)**, **Kaplan NCLEX-RN Prep**, and **LaCharity PDA**.

items: Foods and things to avoid Symptoms of the allergy Mild contact dermatitis Moderately severe symptoms of rhinitis, Conjunctivitis Urticaria Bronchospasm to severe life-threatening anaphylaxis.
Epinephrine This is an adrenaline hormone produced by your body when under stress or experiencing trauma such as an injury or heart attack by increasing blood flow throughout the body.
A) Contact dermatitis B) Latex allergy C) Skin irritation D) Allergic reaction to soap.
Elite nurses’ forum Over view Our immune system is your body’s defense against infections and other harmful invaders. Without it, you would constantly get sick from bacteria or viruses.
Your immune system is made up of special cells, tissues, and organs that work together to protect you.
The lymph, or lymphatic, system is a major part of the immune system. It's a network of lymph nodes and vessels.
Lymphatic vessels are thin tubes that branch, like blood vessels, throughout the body. They carry a clear fluid called lymph.
Lymph contains tissue fluid, waste products, and immune system cells.
Lymph nodes are small, bean-shaped clumps of immune system cells that are connected by lymphatic vessels.
They contain white blood cells that trap viruses, bacteria, and other invaders, including cancer cells.

blocks.title: Immune Hypersensitivity, Anaphylaxis & HIV Care
rows: **Anaphylaxis (Type I IgE)**
Stridor, wheezing, angioedema, urticaria, hypotension.
**IM Epinephrine (1:1000)** into vastus lateralis immediately + O2 + IV 0.9% NS.
**Latex Allergy**
Cross-reactivity with **bananas, avocados, kiwis, chestnuts**.
Screen all clients prior to surgery/catheterization; use latex-free gloves & equipment.
**HIV/AIDS (CD4 < 200)**
Risk for Pneumocystis (PCP), TB, Kaposi sarcoma, candidiasis.
Strict **ART adherence** (>95% doses); TMP-SMX (Bactrim) prophylaxis when CD4 < 200.

items: Lymphatic vessels are thin tubes that branch, like blood vessels, throughout the body. They carry a clear fluid called lymph.
Lymph contains tissue fluid, waste products, and immune system cells.
Lymph nodes are small, bean-shaped clumps of immune system cells that are connected by lymphatic vessels.
They contain white blood cells that trap viruses, bacteria, and other invaders, including cancer cells.
White blood cells are the cells of the immune system. They are made in one of your lymph organs, the bone marrow. Other lymph organs include the spleen and thymus.
When your immune system doesn't work the way it should, it is called an immune system disorder.

Immune system disorders Autoimmune Disorders Description In autoimmune diseases, the body attacks normal, healthy tissues. The cause is unknown. It is probably a combination of a person’s genes and something in the environment that triggers those genes.

quiz.prompt: A healthcare worker experiences hives and itching after using latex gloves. What is the likely diagnosis?
options: Contact dermatitis
Latex allergy
Skin irritation
Allergic reaction to soap.
quiz.rationale: Correct answer: Latex allergy (Verified from Immune problems of the Adult.pptx and Saunders 9th Ed.).

options: Stridor, wheezing, angioedema, urticaria, hypotension.

items: Elite nurses’ forum Over view Our immune system is your body’s defense against infections and other harmful invaders. Without it, you would constantly get sick from bacteria or viruses.
Your immune system is made up of special cells, tissues, and organs that work together to protect you.
The lymph, or lymphatic, system is a major part of the immune system. It's a network of lymph nodes and vessels.
Lymphatic vessels are thin tubes that branch, like blood vessels, throughout the body. They carry a clear fluid called lymph.
Lymph contains tissue fluid, waste products, and immune system cells.
Lymph nodes are small, bean-shaped clumps of immune system cells that are connected by lymphatic vessels.
They contain white blood cells that trap viruses, bacteria, and other invaders, including cancer cells.
White blood cells are the cells of the immune system. They are made in one of your lymph organs, the bone marrow. Other lymph organs include the spleen and thymus.
When your immune system doesn't work the way it should, it is called an immune system disorder.

Immune system disorders Autoimmune Disorders Description In autoimmune diseases, the body attacks normal, healthy tissues. The cause is unknown. It is probably a combination of a person’s genes and something in the environment that triggers those genes.

items: Methotrexate is a drug that is used to help treat rheumatoid arthritis, psoriasis, Crohn’s disease, and some cancers. It works by blocking a chemical in the body that slows the process of cell growth.

Cyclosporine This is another drug used to treat certain cancers, but it can also be used to help prevent organ rejection after an organ transplant. It works by stopping the immune system from attacking foreign bodies like transplanted organs or tissues.

Azathioprine This is another immunosuppressant drug that can be used to prevent organ rejection after transplantation. It works by stopping the immune system from attacking foreign bodies like transplanted organs or tissues.

An antibiotic
questions.rationale: Mucolytic medications help to thin and loosen mucus in the airways, making it easier to cough up. This can be helpful for patients with cystic fibrosis, who often have thick, sticky mucus in their lungs.

questions.prompt: A nurse is caring for a patient who is experiencing visual hallucinations. Which of the following is an appropriate response from the nurse?
options: "There's nothing there, you're just imagining things."
"I understand that you're seeing something, but I do not see it."
"You must be very scared, let me give you something to calm down."
"Why don't you try closing your eyes and see if it goes away?"
questions.rationale: Correct answer: "I understand that you're seeing something, but I do not see it." (Verified from eye and ear  QNS.docx and Saunders 9th Ed.).

questions.prompt: A patient with hypothyroidism is taking levothyroxine. What is the primary goal of treatment?
options: Increase thyroid hormone production
Decrease thyroid hormone production
Regulate metabolism
Reduce weight
questions.rationale: Levothyroxine replaces deficient thyroid hormones.

questions.prompt: A patient with multiple endocrine neoplasia (MEN) is experiencing symptoms of pancreatic cancer. What is the primary goal of treatment?
options: Decrease calcium levels
Increase calcium levels
Regulate pancreatic function
Reduce tumor size
questions.rationale: Treatment aims to reduce tumor size.

questions.prompt: A nurse is caring for a patient who is 2 days post-op from a thoracotomy. The patient is reluctant to perform deep breathing exercises due to pain. Which of the following interventions should the nurse implement?
options: Administer pain medication before the exercises
Encourage shallow breathing to prevent discomfort
Discontinue the exercises until the pain subsides
Encourage the patient to hold their breath as long as possible
questions.rationale: Deep breathing exercises are critical after thoracotomy to prevent complications such as pneumonia and atelectasis. Administering pain medication before the exercises can help alleviate the patient's discomfort and encourage compliance.

questions.prompt: A nurse is caring for a patient who has a tracheostomy. Which of the following interventions would the nurse include in the plan of care to prevent a common complication associated with a tracheostomy?
options: Frequent oral care
Encourage ambulation
Turn the patient every 2 hours
Provide a high protein diet
questions.rationale: Frequent oral care helps to prevent infections, a common complication associated with a tracheostomy.

questions.prompt: A patient with type 1 diabetes is experiencing hyperglycemia. Which medication would the nurse administer?
options: Regular insulin
NPH insulin
Metformin
Glipizide
questions.rationale: Regular insulin is fast-acting, helping to quickly lower blood glucose levels.

questions.prompt: A patient with hypothyroidism is experiencing fatigue and weight gain. What is the nurse's first action?
options: Increase levothyroxine dose
Check thyroid-stimulating hormone (TSH) levels
Encourage exercise
Provide emotional support
questions.rationale: Checking TSH levels helps assess hypothyroidism severity and guides levothyroxine dose adjustments.

questions.prompt: A 10-year-old child is diagnosed with Crohn’s disease. The nurse is teaching the child's parent about nutritional needs. Which of the following statements is correct?
options: "Your child should follow a low-protein diet."
"Your child should avoid eating fruits and vegetables."
"Your child should consume a high-calorie, high-protein diet."
"Your child should limit fluid intake."
questions.rationale: Children with Crohn’s disease often need extra calories and protein to help maintain their weight and support growth. A low-protein diet (option A) and limiting fluid intake (option D) are not typically recommended. Although certain raw fruits and vegetables might need to be avoided during flare-ups due to their high fiber content, they are usually not completely eliminated from the diet (option B).

questions.prompt: A patient presents with a sudden onset of dyspnea. The nurse auscultates the lung and hears a high-pitched sound on inspiration. What could this indicate?
options: Stridor
Crackles
Wheezing
Pleural friction rub
questions.rationale: Stridor is a high-pitched, inspiratory sound that is often heard in acute laryngeal obstruction. It is a medical emergency and requires immediate attention.

questions.prompt: A 15-year-old child with Type 1 Diabetes Mellitus is admitted to the hospital for diabetic ketoacidosis (DKA). Which of the following would the nurse expect to observe?
options: Hypoglycemia
Bradycardia
Kussmaul respirations
Decreased urine output
questions.rationale: Kussmaul respirations (rapid, deep breathing) are a common symptom of DKA, as the body tries to compensate for metabolic acidosis by blowing off excess carbon dioxide. Hypoglycemia (option A) is not typically associated with DKA; instead, blood glucose levels are usually high. Bradycardia (option B) and decreased urine output (option D) are not typical symptoms of DKA.

questions.prompt: A nurse is caring for a patient post bronchoscopy. Which of the following is the most important assessment before offering the patient food or drink?
options: Vital signs
Oxygen saturation
Level of consciousness
Return of the gag reflex
questions.rationale: After a bronchoscopy, the patient’s throat may be numb from local anaesthetics used during the procedure. It is essential to ensure the return of the gag reflex before offering food or drink to prevent aspiration.

questions.prompt: The nurse is caring for a child with suspected appendicitis. Which of the following symptoms would the nurse expect?
options: Left lower quadrant pain
Constipation
Right lower quadrant pain
Diarrhea
questions.rationale: Right lower quadrant pain is a classic symptom of appendicitis. Although constipation (option B) and diarrhea (option D) can occur, they are not as specific to appendicitis. Left lower quadrant pain (option A) is not typically associated with appendicitis.

questions.prompt: A patient with acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS) is intubated and receiving mechanical ventilation. The nurse notices a sudden drop in the patient's oxygen saturation. What should the nurse do first?
options: Increase the fraction of inspired oxygen (FiO2) on the ventilator
Check the ventilator tubing for disconnection or kinks
Suction the endotracheal tube
Notify the physician
questions.rationale: The nurse should first check for any mechanical causes of decreased oxygen saturation, such as a disconnection or kinks in the ventilator tubing, which could compromise ventilation.

questions.prompt: A nurse is caring for a client with tuberculosis. Which of the following actions should the nurse take to prevent the spread of the disease?
options: Wear a mask when providing direct patient care
Place the patient in a private room
Wash hands after removing gloves
All of the above
questions.rationale: Tuberculosis is an airborne disease. It is crucial to wear a mask, place the patient in a private room, and wash hands after removing gloves to prevent the spread of the disease.

questions.prompt: A patient with asthma has been prescribed a metered-dose inhaler (MDI). What instruction should the nurse provide to the patient about using the MDI?
options: Inhale quickly and deeply
Exhale fully before using the MDI
Hold the breath for 10 seconds after inhaling the medication
All of the above
questions.rationale: All of these instructions are correct and help ensure the medication is inhaled into the lungs effectively.

questions.prompt: A patient who was recently in a car accident is having difficulty breathing. The nurse hears a grating sound during both inspiration and expiration. What could this indicate?
options: Normal lung sounds
Pneumothorax
Pleural effusion
Pleural friction rub
questions.rationale: Pleural friction rub is a grating sound produced when inflamed pleural surfaces rub together during respiration. This can occur in conditions such as pleuritis, which can result from trauma such as a car accident.

questions.prompt: A nurse is caring for a patient with pneumonia. Which of the following interventions should the nurse prioritize?
options: Encourage ambulation
Administer antibiotics as prescribed
Maintain a patent airway
Promote fluid intake
questions.rationale: Maintaining a patent airway is the priority nursing intervention for a patient with pneumonia because pneumonia can cause mucus production that can obstruct the airway.

questions.prompt: A patient has been diagnosed with sensorineural hearing loss. Which of the following statements is true about this condition?
options: It is caused by damage to the outer or middle ear.
It is usually reversible with treatment.
It is most often caused by loud noise exposure.
It can be corrected with a cochlear implant.
questions.rationale: Correct answer: It is most often caused by loud noise exposure. (Verified from eye and ear  QNS.docx and Saunders 9th Ed.).

questions.prompt: A nurse is caring for a patient with a diagnosis of emphysema. The nurse would expect to find which of the following during the physical assessment?
options: Increased anterior-posterior diameter
Decreased chest expansion
Fine crackles on auscultation
Hypoventilation
questions.rationale: Emphysema is characterized by an increased anterior-posterior diameter (often referred to as "barrel chest") due to hyperinflation of the alveoli.

questions.prompt: Question: A child with haemophilia falls and sustains a minor injury. What is the nurse's priority action?
options: Apply a cold compress to the injured area
Administer pain medication as ordered
Immediately call the provider
Inspect for signs of internal bleeding
questions.rationale: Correct answer: Apply a cold compress to the injured area (Verified from PAEDIATRIC QUESTIONS.docx and Saunders 9th Ed.).

questions.prompt: A patient with hypothyroidism is experiencing depression. What is the nurse's first action?
options: Increase levothyroxine dose
Check thyroid-stimulating hormone (TSH) levels
Encourage exercise
Provide emotional support
questions.rationale: TSH level assessment guides levothyroxine dose adjustments.

questions.prompt: A 3-year-old child weighing 15 kg is prescribed a medication at a dose of 50 mg/kg/day in 4 divided doses. How many milligrams of the medication will the nurse administer per dose?
options: 75 mg
100 mg
200 mg
questions.rationale: Correct answer: 187.5 mg (Verified from PAEDIATRIC QUESTIONS.docx and Saunders 9th Ed.).

questions.prompt: A nurse is providing discharge instructions to the parents of a child who has undergone chemotherapy. Which of the following instructions should be included?
options: "Your child should avoid crowds and people with infections."
"Your child can return to school and engage in physical activities."
"Your child should eat a diet high in raw fruits and vegetables."
"Your child can receive live virus vaccines."
questions.rationale: Children who have undergone chemotherapy have a suppressed immune system and are more susceptible to infections. They should avoid crowds and people with infections to minimize the risk of getting sick.

questions.prompt: A 10-year-old child with a brain tumor is scared about an upcoming surgery. Which of the following is the most appropriate nursing action?
options: Reassure the child that everything will be okay
Explain the procedure in medical terms
Use simple, age-appropriate language to explain the procedure
Tell the child not to worry because the doctors are very good
questions.rationale: The best approach when communicating with a child is to use simple, age-appropriate language to explain procedures. This can help alleviate fears and anxiety. Options A and D may minimize the child's feelings, while option B may be too complex for a 10-year-old to understand.

questions.prompt: Question: A 2-month-old infant is brought to the clinic with a rash on the scalp characterized by greasy, yellow scales. The nurse should document this finding as which of the following?
options: Seborrheic dermatitis (cradle cap)
Atopic dermatitis (eczema)
Tinea capitis (ringworm)
Impetigo
questions.rationale: Correct answer: Seborrheic dermatitis (cradle cap) (Verified from PAEDIATRIC QUESTIONS.docx and Saunders 9th Ed.).

questions.prompt: A patient with acromegaly is experiencing joint pain and swelling. What is the nurse's first action?
options: Administer octreotide
Check growth hormone levels
Encourage exercise
Provide emotional support
questions.rationale: Octreotide inhibits growth hormone release, alleviating symptoms.

items: GASTROINTESTINAL MEDICATIONS PREPARED BY; CYNTHIA KENOR-KRN/USRN React with gastric acid to produce neutral salts or salts of low acidity. These medications are used for peptic ulcer disease and gastro esophageal reflux disease.

Bleeding of pancreas - Cullen’s sign at umbilicus Predisposing factors 1.
Alcoholism – stimulates release of histamine = Parietal cell release Hcl acid = ulceration 5.

rows: **Cirrhosis & Hepatic Encephalopathy**
High **Ammonia**, **asterixis (flapping tremor)**, ascites, esophageal varices.
Give **Lactulose** (titrate to **2–3 soft stools/day** to excrete ammonia!); prevent bleeding/straining.

RLQ McBurney's point pain; sudden relief + rigid abdomen = perforation!
**NPO**, NO heat pack & NO laxatives/enemas prior to surgical evaluation.

Healthy stoma is **beefy red/pink & moist**; pale/dusky/black = ischemia!
Report black/necrotic stoma immediately; empty pouch when **1/3 to 1/2 full**.

Sucralfate coats ulcers; Omeprazole/Pantoprazole suppress acid.

quiz.prompt: A nurse cares for a client presenting with Cirrhosis & Hepatic Encephalopathy (GERD, Peptic Ulcer Disease, Upper GI Bleed & NG Tube Care). What is the priority nursing action?
options: Administer sedatives or diuretics without reviewing baseline labs or vitals.
Delegate acute clinical assessment and teaching to UAP/CNA.
High Ammonia, asterixis (flapping tremor), ascites, esophageal varices.
Wait 4 hours to reassess before taking any action or documenting.
quiz.rationale: For Cirrhosis & Hepatic Encephalopathy, the priority intervention is: High Ammonia, asterixis (flapping tremor), ascites, esophageal varices. Key exam watchpoint: Give Lactulose (titrate to 2–3 soft stools/day to excrete ammonia!); prevent bleeding/straining.

quiz.prompt: Which statement reflects an unsafe error (or NCLEX trap) that the nurse must AVOID when managing Cirrhosis & Hepatic Encephalopathy?
options: High Ammonia, asterixis (flapping tremor), ascites, esophageal varices.
Monitor vital signs, airway, and target labs closely during care of Cirrhosis & Hepatic Encephalopathy.
Use closed-loop SBAR communication when escalating abnormal clinical changes.
Give Lactulose (titrate to 2–3 soft stools/day to excrete ammonia!); prevent bleeding/straining.
quiz.rationale: When caring for Cirrhosis & Hepatic Encephalopathy, avoiding this unsafe action is critical: Give Lactulose (titrate to 2–3 soft stools/day to excrete ammonia!); prevent bleeding/straining.

quiz.prompt: A nurse cares for a client presenting with Appendicitis & Peritonitis (GERD, Peptic Ulcer Disease, Upper GI Bleed & NG Tube Care). What is the priority nursing action?
options: RLQ McBurney's point pain; sudden relief + rigid abdomen = perforation!
Delegate acute clinical assessment and teaching to UAP/CNA.
Wait 4 hours to reassess before taking any action or documenting.
Administer sedatives or diuretics without reviewing baseline labs or vitals.
quiz.rationale: For Appendicitis & Peritonitis, the priority intervention is: RLQ McBurney's point pain; sudden relief + rigid abdomen = perforation! Key exam watchpoint: NPO, NO heat pack & NO laxatives/enemas prior to surgical evaluation.

quiz.prompt: A nurse cares for a client presenting with Ostomy Care (GERD, Peptic Ulcer Disease, Upper GI Bleed & NG Tube Care). What is the priority nursing action?
options: Administer sedatives or diuretics without reviewing baseline labs or vitals.
Wait 4 hours to reassess before taking any action or documenting.
Delegate acute clinical assessment and teaching to UAP/CNA.
Healthy stoma is beefy red/pink & moist; pale/dusky/black = ischemia!
quiz.rationale: For Ostomy Care, the priority intervention is: Healthy stoma is beefy red/pink & moist; pale/dusky/black = ischemia! Key exam watchpoint: Report black/necrotic stoma immediately; empty pouch when 1/3 to 1/2 full.

quiz.prompt: A nurse cares for a client presenting with Sucralfate & PPIs (GERD, Peptic Ulcer Disease, Upper GI Bleed & NG Tube Care). What is the priority nursing action?
options: Sucralfate coats ulcers; Omeprazole/Pantoprazole suppress acid.
Administer sedatives or diuretics without reviewing baseline labs or vitals.
Delegate acute clinical assessment and teaching to UAP/CNA.
Wait 4 hours to reassess before taking any action or documenting.
quiz.rationale: For Sucralfate & PPIs, the priority intervention is: Sucralfate coats ulcers; Omeprazole/Pantoprazole suppress acid. Key exam watchpoint: Give Sucralfate 1 hr before meals/other meds; PPIs before breakfast.

quiz.prompt: A client managed for GERD, Peptic Ulcer Disease, Upper GI Bleed & NG Tube Care develops sudden tachypnea (RR 32/min), SpO2 87%, and new-onset restlessness. What should the nurse do FIRST?
options: Ask the UAP to assist the client to ambulate in the hallway.
Elevate the head of the bed, assess airway/lung sounds, and apply supplemental oxygen.
Document the vital signs and recheck oxygen saturation in 2 hours.
Administer a PRN opioid analgesic for restlessness before assessing.
quiz.rationale: Under Maslow's hierarchy and ABC prioritization in GERD, Peptic Ulcer Disease, Upper GI Bleed & NG Tube Care, airway and oxygenation cues (SpO2 87%, RR 32, hypoxia-induced restlessness) require immediate airway/O2 support first.

quiz.prompt: Which client care task related to GERD, Peptic Ulcer Disease, Upper GI Bleed & NG Tube Care is appropriate to delegate to an Unlicensed Assistive Personnel (UAP)?
options: Providing initial discharge teaching on red-flag warning signs.
Performing the comprehensive admission assessment for a newly arrived acute client.
Obtaining routine vital signs and strictly measuring oral intake and urine output on a stable client.
Evaluating the client's therapeutic response to an intravenous high-alert medication.
quiz.rationale: Per LaCharity PDA and NCSBN delegation rules, UAPs perform routine, stable data collection (vitals, I&O, ADLs), while assessment, teaching, and evaluation remain RN-only duties.

quiz.prompt: A preceptor reviews discharge teaching for a client recovering under GERD, Peptic Ulcer Disease, Upper GI Bleed & NG Tube Care. Which statement by the client indicates teaching was effective?
options: "I will monitor for warning signs like fever, worsening shortness of breath, or bleeding and contact my provider promptly."
"I do not need follow-up lab monitoring because my hospital discharge labs were normal."
"It is fine to take over-the-counter NSAIDs alongside my prescribed anticoagulants without asking."
"Once I feel a little better tomorrow, I can stop taking all prescribed medications."
quiz.rationale: Effective client education in GERD, Peptic Ulcer Disease, Upper GI Bleed & NG Tube Care requires adherence to therapy, scheduled lab follow-ups, and prompt reporting of acute deterioration.

quiz.prompt: When using the NCSBN 6-Step Clinical Judgment Model (CJMM) for a client in Course Unit 9: Gastrointestinal, Hepatobiliary Disorders & GI Medications, what directly follows 'Recognize Cues' and 'Analyze Cues'?
options: Evaluate Outcomes prior to implementing any bedside intervention.
Delegate hypothesis ranking to support staff before completing assessment.
Prioritize Hypotheses — ranking immediate life-threatening complications first.
Archive the admission chart without creating a care plan.
quiz.rationale: The 6 steps of the NCSBN CJMM progress in order: Recognize Cues -> Analyze Cues -> Prioritize Hypotheses -> Generate Solutions -> Take Action -> Evaluate Outcomes.

quiz.prompt: A patient is experiencing vertigo. The nurse knows that this symptom is likely related to a problem with what part of the sensory system?
options: Visual system
Vestibular system
Olfactory system
Tactile system
quiz.rationale: The vestibular system (B), located within the inner ear, is responsible for maintaining balance and spatial orientation. Vertigo, a sensation of feeling off balance, is often caused by problems in this system. The visual (A), olfactory (C), and tactile (D) systems are not typically associated with symptoms of vertigo.

quiz.prompt: As a nurse leader, you notice that one of your team members is consistently late for their shift. What is the most appropriate action?
options: Ignore the behavior as it doesn't affect patient care.
Report the behavior to the hospital administration.
Discuss the issue with the team member privately.
Publicly reprimand the team member during a staff meeting.
quiz.rationale: In this situation, the most appropriate action for a nurse leader is to address the issue directly with the individual involved (C). Ignoring the behavior (A) is not an effective leadership strategy as it fails to address the issue. Reporting the behavior to administration (B) should be a last resort if the behavior continues after addressing it directly. Publicly reprimanding the team member (D) is not appropriate and could create a hostile work environment.

quiz.prompt: As a nurse leader, you are implementing a change in a hospital protocol. What is the best way to ensure staff compliance with this change?
options: Enforce strict punishments for non-compliance.
Communicate the rationale for the change.
Make the change without explaining why.
Implement the change without seeking staff input.
quiz.rationale: Effective leadership involves open and clear communication. Explaining the rationale for the change (B) helps staff understand the importance and necessity of the change, thereby fostering compliance. Enforcing strict punishments (A) tends to create a negative work environment. Implementing a change without explanation (C) or without seeking staff input (D) can lead to resistance and non-compliance.

quiz.prompt: A nurse is teaching a patient who has been diagnosed with glaucoma. Which of the following statements by the patient indicates the need for further teaching?
options: "I will need to use my eye drops daily."
"I will avoid straining during bowel movements."
"I am glad I can stop taking my eye drops once my symptoms improve."
"I understand that I will need regular check-ups for my eye pressure."
quiz.rationale: Correct answer: "I am glad I can stop taking my eye drops once my symptoms improve." (Verified from eye and ear  QNS.docx and Saunders 9th Ed.).

quiz.prompt: A nurse is providing leadership training to a group of new graduate nurses. Which of the following leadership styles is likely to be most effective for promoting autonomy and critical thinking among the new nurses?
options: Autocratic
Laissez-faire
Democratic
Transactional
quiz.rationale: Correct answer: Democratic (Verified from eye and ear  QNS.docx and Saunders 9th Ed.).

quiz.prompt: A nurse is assessing a patient with suspected macular degeneration. Which of the following findings would most likely indicate this condition?
options: Loss of peripheral vision
Difficulty distinguishing colors
Blurred vision
Central vision loss
quiz.rationale: Correct answer: Central vision loss (Verified from eye and ear  QNS.docx and Saunders 9th Ed.).

quiz.prompt: As a nurse leader, you observe a conflict between two team members. What is the most appropriate initial action?
options: Ignore the conflict and hope it resolves itself.
Immediately report the incident to higher management.
Facilitate a meeting between the two individuals to discuss the issue.
Take sides with the person who has been with the team longer.
quiz.rationale: Correct answer: Facilitate a meeting between the two individuals to discuss the issue. (Verified from eye and ear  QNS.docx and Saunders 9th Ed.).

quiz.prompt: A patient with diabetes reports experiencing numbness and tingling in their feet. This is most likely indicative of which of the following conditions?
options: Diabetic retinopathy
Diabetic neuropathy
Diabetic nephropathy
Diabetic ketoacidosis
quiz.rationale: Correct answer: Diabetic neuropathy (Verified from eye and ear  QNS.docx and Saunders 9th Ed.).

quiz.prompt: A patient with a history of glaucoma has been prescribed eye drops to decrease intraocular pressure. The patient also has other chronic conditions that require medication. Which of the following should be the nurse's priority instruction?
options: "Take your glaucoma eye drops first before any other medication."
"You can take your glaucoma eye drops at the same time as your other medications."
"Take your glaucoma eye drops last after all other medications."
"The timing of your glaucoma eye drops in relation to other medications doesn't matter."
quiz.rationale: Correct answer: "Take your glaucoma eye drops first before any other medication." (Verified from eye and ear  QNS.docx and Saunders 9th Ed.).

quiz.prompt: A nurse is prioritizing care for a patient who has been newly diagnosed with Meniere's disease. Which of the following should be the nurse's first action?
options: Providing patient education about the disease
Starting the patient on a low-sodium diet
Administering prescribed medication
Assessing the patient's current level of knowledge
quiz.rationale: Correct answer: Assessing the patient's current level of knowledge (Verified from eye and ear  QNS.docx and Saunders 9th Ed.).

quiz.prompt: A patient with a spinal cord injury report experiencing phantom limb pain. The nurse should prioritize which of the following interventions?
options: Administering prescribed pain medication
Reassuring the patient that the pain is not real
Teaching the patient distraction techniques
Assessing the patient's pain level and characteristics
quiz.rationale: Correct answer: Assessing the patient's pain level and characteristics (Verified from eye and ear  QNS.docx and Saunders 9th Ed.).

questions.prompt: Which client care task related to GI Pharmacology: PPIs, H2 Blockers, Sucralfate, Lactulose & Antiemetics is appropriate to delegate to an Unlicensed Assistive Personnel (UAP)?
options: Obtaining routine vital signs and strictly measuring oral intake and urine output on a stable client.
Evaluating the client's therapeutic response to an intravenous high-alert medication.
Performing the comprehensive admission assessment for a newly arrived acute client.
Providing initial discharge teaching on red-flag warning signs.
questions.rationale: Per LaCharity PDA and NCSBN delegation rules, UAPs perform routine, stable data collection (vitals, I&O, ADLs), while assessment, teaching, and evaluation remain RN-only duties.

questions.prompt: A nurse is prioritizing care for a patient who has been newly diagnosed with Meniere's disease. Which of the following should be the nurse's first action?
options: Providing patient education about the disease
Starting the patient on a low-sodium diet
Administering prescribed medication
Assessing the patient's current level of knowledge
questions.rationale: Correct answer: Assessing the patient's current level of knowledge (Verified from eye and ear  QNS.docx and Saunders 9th Ed.).

questions.prompt: A patient with diabetes reports experiencing numbness and tingling in their feet. This is most likely indicative of which of the following conditions?
options: Diabetic retinopathy
Diabetic neuropathy
Diabetic nephropathy
Diabetic ketoacidosis
questions.rationale: Correct answer: Diabetic neuropathy (Verified from eye and ear  QNS.docx and Saunders 9th Ed.).

questions.prompt: A patient with a spinal cord injury report experiencing phantom limb pain. The nurse should prioritize which of the following interventions?
options: Administering prescribed pain medication
Reassuring the patient that the pain is not real
Teaching the patient distraction techniques
Assessing the patient's pain level and characteristics
questions.rationale: Correct answer: Assessing the patient's pain level and characteristics (Verified from eye and ear  QNS.docx and Saunders 9th Ed.).

questions.prompt: A client managed for GERD, Peptic Ulcer Disease, Upper GI Bleed & NG Tube Care develops sudden tachypnea (RR 32/min), SpO2 87%, and new-onset restlessness. What should the nurse do FIRST?
options: Ask the UAP to assist the client to ambulate in the hallway.
Elevate the head of the bed, assess airway/lung sounds, and apply supplemental oxygen.
Document the vital signs and recheck oxygen saturation in 2 hours.
Administer a PRN opioid analgesic for restlessness before assessing.
questions.rationale: Under Maslow's hierarchy and ABC prioritization in GERD, Peptic Ulcer Disease, Upper GI Bleed & NG Tube Care, airway and oxygenation cues (SpO2 87%, RR 32, hypoxia-induced restlessness) require immediate airway/O2 support first.

questions.prompt: A nurse cares for a client presenting with Sucralfate & PPIs (IBD (Crohn's vs. UC), Bowel Obstruction, Ostomies, Cirrhosis & Pancreatitis). What is the priority nursing action?
options: Wait 4 hours to reassess before taking any action or documenting.
Sucralfate coats ulcers; Omeprazole/Pantoprazole suppress acid.
Administer sedatives or diuretics without reviewing baseline labs or vitals.
Delegate acute clinical assessment and teaching to UAP/CNA.
questions.rationale: For Sucralfate & PPIs, the priority intervention is: Sucralfate coats ulcers; Omeprazole/Pantoprazole suppress acid. Key exam watchpoint: Give Sucralfate 1 hr before meals/other meds; PPIs before breakfast.

questions.prompt: A nurse cares for a client presenting with Appendicitis & Peritonitis (GERD, Peptic Ulcer Disease, Upper GI Bleed & NG Tube Care). What is the priority nursing action?
options: RLQ McBurney's point pain; sudden relief + rigid abdomen = perforation!
Delegate acute clinical assessment and teaching to UAP/CNA.
Wait 4 hours to reassess before taking any action or documenting.
Administer sedatives or diuretics without reviewing baseline labs or vitals.
questions.rationale: For Appendicitis & Peritonitis, the priority intervention is: RLQ McBurney's point pain; sudden relief + rigid abdomen = perforation! Key exam watchpoint: NPO, NO heat pack & NO laxatives/enemas prior to surgical evaluation.

questions.prompt: A preceptor reviews discharge teaching for a client recovering under GI Pharmacology: PPIs, H2 Blockers, Sucralfate, Lactulose & Antiemetics. Which statement by the client indicates teaching was effective?
options: "It is fine to take over-the-counter NSAIDs alongside my prescribed anticoagulants without asking."
"I do not need follow-up lab monitoring because my hospital discharge labs were normal."
"Once I feel a little better tomorrow, I can stop taking all prescribed medications."
"I will monitor for warning signs like fever, worsening shortness of breath, or bleeding and contact my provider promptly."
questions.rationale: Effective client education in GI Pharmacology: PPIs, H2 Blockers, Sucralfate, Lactulose & Antiemetics requires adherence to therapy, scheduled lab follow-ups, and prompt reporting of acute deterioration.

questions.prompt: When using the NCSBN 6-Step Clinical Judgment Model (CJMM) for a client in Course Unit 9: Gastrointestinal, Hepatobiliary Disorders & GI Medications, what directly follows 'Recognize Cues' and 'Analyze Cues'?
options: Prioritize Hypotheses — ranking immediate life-threatening complications first.
Archive the admission chart without creating a care plan.
Evaluate Outcomes prior to implementing any bedside intervention.
Delegate hypothesis ranking to support staff before completing assessment.
questions.rationale: The 6 steps of the NCSBN CJMM progress in order: Recognize Cues -> Analyze Cues -> Prioritize Hypotheses -> Generate Solutions -> Take Action -> Evaluate Outcomes.

questions.prompt: As a nurse leader, you are implementing a change in a hospital protocol. What is the best way to ensure staff compliance with this change?
options: Enforce strict punishments for non-compliance.
Communicate the rationale for the change.
Make the change without explaining why.
Implement the change without seeking staff input.
questions.rationale: Effective leadership involves open and clear communication. Explaining the rationale for the change (B) helps staff understand the importance and necessity of the change, thereby fostering compliance. Enforcing strict punishments (A) tends to create a negative work environment. Implementing a change without explanation (C) or without seeking staff input (D) can lead to resistance and non-compliance.

questions.prompt: A nurse is providing leadership training to a group of new graduate nurses. Which of the following leadership styles is likely to be most effective for promoting autonomy and critical thinking among the new nurses?
options: Autocratic
Laissez-faire
Democratic
Transactional
questions.rationale: Correct answer: Democratic (Verified from eye and ear  QNS.docx and Saunders 9th Ed.).

questions.prompt: As a nurse leader, you observe a conflict between two team members. What is the most appropriate initial action?
options: Ignore the conflict and hope it resolves itself.
Immediately report the incident to higher management.
Facilitate a meeting between the two individuals to discuss the issue.
Take sides with the person who has been with the team longer.
questions.rationale: Correct answer: Facilitate a meeting between the two individuals to discuss the issue. (Verified from eye and ear  QNS.docx and Saunders 9th Ed.).

options: Providing initial discharge teaching on red-flag warning signs.
Performing the comprehensive admission assessment for a newly arrived acute client.
Obtaining routine vital signs and strictly measuring oral intake and urine output on a stable client.
Evaluating the client's therapeutic response to an intravenous high-alert medication.
questions.rationale: Per LaCharity PDA and NCSBN delegation rules, UAPs perform routine, stable data collection (vitals, I&O, ADLs), while assessment, teaching, and evaluation remain RN-only duties.

questions.prompt: A client managed for IBD (Crohn's vs. UC), Bowel Obstruction, Ostomies, Cirrhosis & Pancreatitis develops sudden tachypnea (RR 32/min), SpO2 87%, and new-onset restlessness. What should the nurse do FIRST?
options: Ask the UAP to assist the client to ambulate in the hallway.
Document the vital signs and recheck oxygen saturation in 2 hours.
Administer a PRN opioid analgesic for restlessness before assessing.
Elevate the head of the bed, assess airway/lung sounds, and apply supplemental oxygen.
questions.rationale: Under Maslow's hierarchy and ABC prioritization in IBD (Crohn's vs. UC), Bowel Obstruction, Ostomies, Cirrhosis & Pancreatitis, airway and oxygenation cues (SpO2 87%, RR 32, hypoxia-induced restlessness) require immediate airway/O2 support first.

questions.prompt: A patient with a history of glaucoma has been prescribed eye drops to decrease intraocular pressure. The patient also has other chronic conditions that require medication. Which of the following should be the nurse's priority instruction?
options: "Take your glaucoma eye drops first before any other medication."
"You can take your glaucoma eye drops at the same time as your other medications."
"Take your glaucoma eye drops last after all other medications."
"The timing of your glaucoma eye drops in relation to other medications doesn't matter."
questions.rationale: Correct answer: "Take your glaucoma eye drops first before any other medication." (Verified from eye and ear  QNS.docx and Saunders 9th Ed.).

questions.prompt: A nurse cares for a client presenting with Cirrhosis & Hepatic Encephalopathy (GERD, Peptic Ulcer Disease, Upper GI Bleed & NG Tube Care). What is the priority nursing action?
options: Administer sedatives or diuretics without reviewing baseline labs or vitals.
Delegate acute clinical assessment and teaching to UAP/CNA.
High Ammonia, asterixis (flapping tremor), ascites, esophageal varices.
Wait 4 hours to reassess before taking any action or documenting.
questions.rationale: For Cirrhosis & Hepatic Encephalopathy, the priority intervention is: High Ammonia, asterixis (flapping tremor), ascites, esophageal varices. Key exam watchpoint: Give Lactulose (titrate to 2–3 soft stools/day to excrete ammonia!); prevent bleeding/straining.

questions.prompt: As a nurse leader, you notice that one of your team members is consistently late for their shift. What is the most appropriate action?
options: Ignore the behavior as it doesn't affect patient care.
Report the behavior to the hospital administration.
Discuss the issue with the team member privately.
Publicly reprimand the team member during a staff meeting.
questions.rationale: In this situation, the most appropriate action for a nurse leader is to address the issue directly with the individual involved (C). Ignoring the behavior (A) is not an effective leadership strategy as it fails to address the issue. Reporting the behavior to administration (B) should be a last resort if the behavior continues after addressing it directly. Publicly reprimanding the team member (D) is not appropriate and could create a hostile work environment.

questions.prompt: A preceptor reviews discharge teaching for a client recovering under IBD (Crohn's vs. UC), Bowel Obstruction, Ostomies, Cirrhosis & Pancreatitis. Which statement by the client indicates teaching was effective?
options: "I will monitor for warning signs like fever, worsening shortness of breath, or bleeding and contact my provider promptly."
"It is fine to take over-the-counter NSAIDs alongside my prescribed anticoagulants without asking."
"I do not need follow-up lab monitoring because my hospital discharge labs were normal."
"Once I feel a little better tomorrow, I can stop taking all prescribed medications."
questions.rationale: Effective client education in IBD (Crohn's vs. UC), Bowel Obstruction, Ostomies, Cirrhosis & Pancreatitis requires adherence to therapy, scheduled lab follow-ups, and prompt reporting of acute deterioration.

questions.prompt: Which statement reflects an unsafe error (or NCLEX trap) that the nurse must AVOID when managing Cirrhosis & Hepatic Encephalopathy?
options: High Ammonia, asterixis (flapping tremor), ascites, esophageal varices.
Monitor vital signs, airway, and target labs closely during care of Cirrhosis & Hepatic Encephalopathy.
Use closed-loop SBAR communication when escalating abnormal clinical changes.
Give Lactulose (titrate to 2–3 soft stools/day to excrete ammonia!); prevent bleeding/straining.
questions.rationale: When caring for Cirrhosis & Hepatic Encephalopathy, avoiding this unsafe action is critical: Give Lactulose (titrate to 2–3 soft stools/day to excrete ammonia!); prevent bleeding/straining.

questions.prompt: A nurse cares for a client presenting with Sucralfate & PPIs (GI Pharmacology: PPIs, H2 Blockers, Sucralfate, Lactulose & Antiemetics). What is the priority nursing action?
options: Delegate acute clinical assessment and teaching to UAP/CNA.
Sucralfate coats ulcers; Omeprazole/Pantoprazole suppress acid.
Wait 4 hours to reassess before taking any action or documenting.
Administer sedatives or diuretics without reviewing baseline labs or vitals.
questions.rationale: For Sucralfate & PPIs, the priority intervention is: Sucralfate coats ulcers; Omeprazole/Pantoprazole suppress acid. Key exam watchpoint: Give Sucralfate 1 hr before meals/other meds; PPIs before breakfast.

questions.prompt: A nurse cares for a client presenting with Ostomy Care (GI Pharmacology: PPIs, H2 Blockers, Sucralfate, Lactulose & Antiemetics). What is the priority nursing action?
options: Healthy stoma is beefy red/pink & moist; pale/dusky/black = ischemia!
Wait 4 hours to reassess before taking any action or documenting.
Delegate acute clinical assessment and teaching to UAP/CNA.
Administer sedatives or diuretics without reviewing baseline labs or vitals.
questions.rationale: For Ostomy Care, the priority intervention is: Healthy stoma is beefy red/pink & moist; pale/dusky/black = ischemia! Key exam watchpoint: Report black/necrotic stoma immediately; empty pouch when 1/3 to 1/2 full.

questions.prompt: A nurse cares for a client presenting with Ostomy Care (GERD, Peptic Ulcer Disease, Upper GI Bleed & NG Tube Care). What is the priority nursing action?
options: Administer sedatives or diuretics without reviewing baseline labs or vitals.
Wait 4 hours to reassess before taking any action or documenting.
Delegate acute clinical assessment and teaching to UAP/CNA.
Healthy stoma is beefy red/pink & moist; pale/dusky/black = ischemia!
questions.rationale: For Ostomy Care, the priority intervention is: Healthy stoma is beefy red/pink & moist; pale/dusky/black = ischemia! Key exam watchpoint: Report black/necrotic stoma immediately; empty pouch when 1/3 to 1/2 full.

questions.prompt: A nurse cares for a client presenting with Sucralfate & PPIs (GERD, Peptic Ulcer Disease, Upper GI Bleed & NG Tube Care). What is the priority nursing action?
options: Sucralfate coats ulcers; Omeprazole/Pantoprazole suppress acid.
Administer sedatives or diuretics without reviewing baseline labs or vitals.
Delegate acute clinical assessment and teaching to UAP/CNA.
Wait 4 hours to reassess before taking any action or documenting.
questions.rationale: For Sucralfate & PPIs, the priority intervention is: Sucralfate coats ulcers; Omeprazole/Pantoprazole suppress acid. Key exam watchpoint: Give Sucralfate 1 hr before meals/other meds; PPIs before breakfast.
