Delay intervention and document Severe Preeclampsia at end of shift.
Delegate initial assessment of Severe Preeclampsia to an unlicensed assistive personnel (UAP).
Ignore abnormal trends in Severe Preeclampsia unless the client requests medication.
questions.rationale: Per Saunders 9th Ed. and Kaplan NCLEX-RN guidelines for Antepartum Care, Preeclampsia (MgSO4), Placenta Previa vs. Abruption, Severe Preeclampsia requires: BP >= 160/110 mmHg, proteinuria, severe headache, visual disturbances, RUQ/epigastric pain.

questions.prompt: A nurse is teaching a patient who has been diagnosed with glaucoma. Which of the following statements by the patient indicates the need for further teaching?
options: "I will need to use my eye drops daily."
"I will avoid straining during bowel movements."
"I am glad I can stop taking my eye drops once my symptoms improve."
"I understand that I will need regular check-ups for my eye pressure."
questions.rationale: Correct answer: "I am glad I can stop taking my eye drops once my symptoms improve." (Verified from eye and ear  QNS.docx and Saunders 9th Ed.).

questions.prompt: A nurse is assessing a patient with suspected macular degeneration. Which of the following findings would most likely indicate this condition?
options: Loss of peripheral vision
Difficulty distinguishing colors
Blurred vision
Central vision loss
questions.rationale: Correct answer: Central vision loss (Verified from eye and ear  QNS.docx and Saunders 9th Ed.).

questions.prompt: A nurse is reviewing clinical protocols for BUBBLE-HE Postpartum Check under Postpartum Hemorrhage (BUBBLE-HE), APGAR Scoring & Newborn Care. Which nursing action is most accurate?
options: Breasts, Uterus, Bladder, Bowel, Lochia (Rubra -> Serosa -> Alba), Episiotomy, Homans/DVT, Emotional status.
Delay intervention and document BUBBLE-HE Postpartum Check at end of shift.
Ignore abnormal trends in BUBBLE-HE Postpartum Check unless the client requests medication.
Delegate initial assessment of BUBBLE-HE Postpartum Check to an unlicensed assistive personnel (UAP).
questions.rationale: Per Saunders 9th Ed. and Kaplan NCLEX-RN guidelines for Postpartum Hemorrhage (BUBBLE-HE), APGAR Scoring & Newborn Care, BUBBLE-HE Postpartum Check requires: Breasts, Uterus, Bladder, Bowel, Lochia (Rubra -> Serosa -> Alba), Episiotomy, Homans/DVT, Emotional status.

questions.prompt: A nurse is providing leadership training to a group of new graduate nurses. Which of the following leadership styles is likely to be most effective for promoting autonomy and critical thinking among the new nurses?
options: Autocratic
Laissez-faire
Democratic
Transactional
questions.rationale: Correct answer: Democratic (Verified from eye and ear  QNS.docx and Saunders 9th Ed.).

questions.prompt: A nurse is prioritizing care for a patient who has been newly diagnosed with Meniere's disease. Which of the following should be the nurse's first action?
options: Providing patient education about the disease
Starting the patient on a low-sodium diet
Administering prescribed medication
Assessing the patient's current level of knowledge
questions.rationale: Correct answer: Assessing the patient's current level of knowledge (Verified from eye and ear  QNS.docx and Saunders 9th Ed.).

questions.prompt: A nurse is caring for a patient who reports a sudden loss of hearing in one ear. Which of the following actions should the nurse take first?
options: Administer prescribed ear drops
Schedule the patient for a hearing test
Report the symptom to the healthcare provider
Clean the patient's ear canal
questions.rationale: Correct answer: Report the symptom to the healthcare provider (Verified from eye and ear  QNS.docx and Saunders 9th Ed.).

questions.prompt: A patient with diabetes reports experiencing numbness and tingling in their feet. This is most likely indicative of which of the following conditions?
options: Diabetic retinopathy
Diabetic neuropathy
Diabetic nephropathy
Diabetic ketoacidosis
questions.rationale: Correct answer: Diabetic neuropathy (Verified from eye and ear  QNS.docx and Saunders 9th Ed.).

questions.prompt: A preceptor reviews discharge teaching for a client recovering under Intrapartum Labour Stages & Fetal Heart Rate Strips (VEAL CHOP). Which statement by the client indicates teaching was effective?
options: "I will monitor for warning signs like fever, worsening shortness of breath, or bleeding and contact my provider promptly."
"It is fine to take over-the-counter NSAIDs alongside my prescribed anticoagulants without asking."
"Once I feel a little better tomorrow, I can stop taking all prescribed medications."
"I do not need follow-up lab monitoring because my hospital discharge labs were normal."
questions.rationale: Effective client education in Intrapartum Labour Stages & Fetal Heart Rate Strips (VEAL CHOP) requires adherence to therapy, scheduled lab follow-ups, and prompt reporting of acute deterioration.

questions.prompt: A nurse is reviewing clinical protocols for Oxytocin (Pitocin) Safety under Intrapartum Labour Stages & Fetal Heart Rate Strips (VEAL CHOP). Which nursing action is most accurate?
options: Discontinue immediately for tachysystole (>5 contractions in 10 min) or late decelerations.
Delegate initial assessment of Oxytocin (Pitocin) Safety to an unlicensed assistive personnel (UAP).
Delay intervention and document Oxytocin (Pitocin) Safety at end of shift.
Ignore abnormal trends in Oxytocin (Pitocin) Safety unless the client requests medication.
questions.rationale: Per Saunders 9th Ed. and Kaplan NCLEX-RN guidelines for Intrapartum Labour Stages & Fetal Heart Rate Strips (VEAL CHOP), Oxytocin (Pitocin) Safety requires: Discontinue immediately for tachysystole (>5 contractions in 10 min) or late decelerations.

questions.prompt: A nurse is reviewing clinical protocols for Normal Baseline FHR under Intrapartum Labour Stages & Fetal Heart Rate Strips (VEAL CHOP). Which nursing action is most accurate?
options: Ignore abnormal trends in Normal Baseline FHR unless the client requests medication.
Delay intervention and document Normal Baseline FHR at end of shift.
Delegate initial assessment of Normal Baseline FHR to an unlicensed assistive personnel (UAP).
110–160 bpm with moderate variability (6–25 bpm).
questions.rationale: Per Saunders 9th Ed. and Kaplan NCLEX-RN guidelines for Intrapartum Labour Stages & Fetal Heart Rate Strips (VEAL CHOP), Normal Baseline FHR requires: 110–160 bpm with moderate variability (6–25 bpm).

questions.prompt: When using the NCSBN 6-Step Clinical Judgment Model (CJMM) for a client in Course Unit 14: Maternity & Newborn Nursing (Antepartum, Labour & Postpartum), what directly follows 'Recognize Cues' and 'Analyze Cues'?
options: Delegate hypothesis ranking to support staff before completing assessment.
Prioritize Hypotheses — ranking immediate life-threatening complications first.
Evaluate Outcomes prior to implementing any bedside intervention.
Archive the admission chart without creating a care plan.
questions.rationale: The 6 steps of the NCSBN CJMM progress in order: Recognize Cues -> Analyze Cues -> Prioritize Hypotheses -> Generate Solutions -> Take Action -> Evaluate Outcomes.

questions.prompt: Which client care task related to Postpartum Hemorrhage (BUBBLE-HE), APGAR Scoring & Newborn Care is appropriate to delegate to an Unlicensed Assistive Personnel (UAP)?
options: Evaluating the client's therapeutic response to an intravenous high-alert medication.
Performing the comprehensive admission assessment for a newly arrived acute client.
Providing initial discharge teaching on red-flag warning signs.
Obtaining routine vital signs and strictly measuring oral intake and urine output on a stable client.
questions.rationale: Per LaCharity PDA and NCSBN delegation rules, UAPs perform routine, stable data collection (vitals, I&O, ADLs), while assessment, teaching, and evaluation remain RN-only duties.

questions.prompt: A nurse is reviewing clinical protocols for Newborn Hypoglycemia (<40–45 mg/dL) under Postpartum Hemorrhage (BUBBLE-HE), APGAR Scoring & Newborn Care. Which nursing action is most accurate?
options: Feed early; watch jitteriness, poor feeding, hypothermia, high-pitched cry.
Delegate initial assessment of Newborn Hypoglycemia (<40–45 mg/dL) to an unlicensed assistive personnel (UAP).
Delay intervention and document Newborn Hypoglycemia (<40–45 mg/dL) at end of shift.
Ignore abnormal trends in Newborn Hypoglycemia (<40–45 mg/dL) unless the client requests medication.
questions.rationale: Per Saunders 9th Ed. and Kaplan NCLEX-RN guidelines for Postpartum Hemorrhage (BUBBLE-HE), APGAR Scoring & Newborn Care, Newborn Hypoglycemia (<40–45 mg/dL) requires: Feed early; watch jitteriness, poor feeding, hypothermia, high-pitched cry.

questions.prompt: A client managed for Antepartum Care, Preeclampsia (MgSO4), Placenta Previa vs. Abruption develops sudden tachypnea (RR 32/min), SpO2 87%, and new-onset restlessness. What should the nurse do FIRST?
options: Administer a PRN opioid analgesic for restlessness before assessing.
Document the vital signs and recheck oxygen saturation in 2 hours.
Elevate the head of the bed, assess airway/lung sounds, and apply supplemental oxygen.
Ask the UAP to assist the client to ambulate in the hallway.
questions.rationale: Under Maslow's hierarchy and ABC prioritization in Antepartum Care, Preeclampsia (MgSO4), Placenta Previa vs. Abruption, airway and oxygenation cues (SpO2 87%, RR 32, hypoxia-induced restlessness) require immediate airway/O2 support first.

questions.prompt: A nurse is reviewing clinical protocols for Postpartum Hemorrhage (>500 mL vaginal / >1000 mL C-section) under Postpartum Hemorrhage (BUBBLE-HE), APGAR Scoring & Newborn Care. Which nursing action is most accurate?
options: First action for boggy uterus is firm fundal massage; assess/empty distended bladder.
Delegate initial assessment of Postpartum Hemorrhage (>500 mL vaginal / >1000 mL C-section) to an unlicensed assistive personnel (UAP).
Delay intervention and document Postpartum Hemorrhage (>500 mL vaginal / >1000 mL C-section) at end of shift.
Ignore abnormal trends in Postpartum Hemorrhage (>500 mL vaginal / >1000 mL C-section) unless the client requests medication.
questions.rationale: Per Saunders 9th Ed. and Kaplan NCLEX-RN guidelines for Postpartum Hemorrhage (BUBBLE-HE), APGAR Scoring & Newborn Care, Postpartum Hemorrhage (>500 mL vaginal / >1000 mL C-section) requires: First action for boggy uterus is firm fundal massage; assess/empty distended bladder.

questions.prompt: A patient with a spinal cord injury report experiencing phantom limb pain. The nurse should prioritize which of the following interventions?
options: Administering prescribed pain medication
Reassuring the patient that the pain is not real
Teaching the patient distraction techniques
Assessing the patient's pain level and characteristics
questions.rationale: Correct answer: Assessing the patient's pain level and characteristics (Verified from eye and ear  QNS.docx and Saunders 9th Ed.).

questions.prompt: Which client care task related to Intrapartum Labour Stages & Fetal Heart Rate Strips (VEAL CHOP) is appropriate to delegate to an Unlicensed Assistive Personnel (UAP)?
options: Performing the comprehensive admission assessment for a newly arrived acute client.
Evaluating the client's therapeutic response to an intravenous high-alert medication.
Obtaining routine vital signs and strictly measuring oral intake and urine output on a stable client.
Providing initial discharge teaching on red-flag warning signs.
questions.rationale: Per LaCharity PDA and NCSBN delegation rules, UAPs perform routine, stable data collection (vitals, I&O, ADLs), while assessment, teaching, and evaluation remain RN-only duties.

questions.prompt: A nurse is reviewing clinical protocols for APGAR at 1 & 5 minutes under Postpartum Hemorrhage (BUBBLE-HE), APGAR Scoring & Newborn Care. Which nursing action is most accurate?
options: Delay intervention and document APGAR at 1 & 5 minutes at end of shift.
Ignore abnormal trends in APGAR at 1 & 5 minutes unless the client requests medication.
Appearance, Pulse (>100), Grimace, Activity, Respiration (7–10 normal; 4–6 moderate distress; 0–3 resuscitate).
Delegate initial assessment of APGAR at 1 & 5 minutes to an unlicensed assistive personnel (UAP).
questions.rationale: Per Saunders 9th Ed. and Kaplan NCLEX-RN guidelines for Postpartum Hemorrhage (BUBBLE-HE), APGAR Scoring & Newborn Care, APGAR at 1 & 5 minutes requires: Appearance, Pulse (>100), Grimace, Activity, Respiration (7–10 normal; 4–6 moderate distress; 0–3 resuscitate).

questions.prompt: A preceptor reviews discharge teaching for a client recovering under Antepartum Care, Preeclampsia (MgSO4), Placenta Previa vs. Abruption. Which statement by the client indicates teaching was effective?
options: "It is fine to take over-the-counter NSAIDs alongside my prescribed anticoagulants without asking."
"Once I feel a little better tomorrow, I can stop taking all prescribed medications."
"I will monitor for warning signs like fever, worsening shortness of breath, or bleeding and contact my provider promptly."
"I do not need follow-up lab monitoring because my hospital discharge labs were normal."
questions.rationale: Effective client education in Antepartum Care, Preeclampsia (MgSO4), Placenta Previa vs. Abruption requires adherence to therapy, scheduled lab follow-ups, and prompt reporting of acute deterioration.

questions.prompt: A nurse is reviewing clinical protocols for Antidote for Magnesium Toxicity under Antepartum Care, Preeclampsia (MgSO4), Placenta Previa vs. Abruption. Which nursing action is most accurate?
options: Ignore abnormal trends in Antidote for Magnesium Toxicity unless the client requests medication.
Keep Calcium Gluconate 10% IV immediately available at the bedside.
Delay intervention and document Antidote for Magnesium Toxicity at end of shift.
Delegate initial assessment of Antidote for Magnesium Toxicity to an unlicensed assistive personnel (UAP).
questions.rationale: Per Saunders 9th Ed. and Kaplan NCLEX-RN guidelines for Antepartum Care, Preeclampsia (MgSO4), Placenta Previa vs. Abruption, Antidote for Magnesium Toxicity requires: Keep Calcium Gluconate 10% IV immediately available at the bedside.

questions.prompt: A nurse is reviewing clinical protocols for Placenta Previa under Antepartum Care, Preeclampsia (MgSO4), Placenta Previa vs. Abruption. Which nursing action is most accurate?
options: Delay intervention and document Placenta Previa at end of shift.
Delegate initial assessment of Placenta Previa to an unlicensed assistive personnel (UAP).
Ignore abnormal trends in Placenta Previa unless the client requests medication.
Painless bright red vaginal bleeding in 2nd/3rd trimester — NEVER perform a digital vaginal exam!
questions.rationale: Per Saunders 9th Ed. and Kaplan NCLEX-RN guidelines for Antepartum Care, Preeclampsia (MgSO4), Placenta Previa vs. Abruption, Placenta Previa requires: Painless bright red vaginal bleeding in 2nd/3rd trimester — NEVER perform a digital vaginal exam!

questions.prompt: A nurse is reviewing clinical protocols for Magnesium Sulfate (MgSO4) under Antepartum Care, Preeclampsia (MgSO4), Placenta Previa vs. Abruption. Which nursing action is most accurate?
options: Delegate initial assessment of Magnesium Sulfate (MgSO4) to an unlicensed assistive personnel (UAP).
Prevents eclamptic seizures; monitor DTRs (absent = hold!), RR >= 12/min, urine output >= 30 mL/hr.
Delay intervention and document Magnesium Sulfate (MgSO4) at end of shift.
Ignore abnormal trends in Magnesium Sulfate (MgSO4) unless the client requests medication.
questions.rationale: Per Saunders 9th Ed. and Kaplan NCLEX-RN guidelines for Antepartum Care, Preeclampsia (MgSO4), Placenta Previa vs. Abruption, Magnesium Sulfate (MgSO4) requires: Prevents eclamptic seizures; monitor DTRs (absent = hold!), RR >= 12/min, urine output >= 30 mL/hr.

questions.prompt: A patient with asthma has been prescribed a corticosteroid inhaler and a bronchodilator inhaler. How should these medications be administered?
options: The bronchodilator should be used, followed by the corticosteroid
The corticosteroid should be used, followed by the bronchodilator
Both inhalers should be used simultaneously
The order of administration does not matter
questions.rationale: The bronchodilator should be administered first to open the airways, allowing the corticosteroid to be more effectively delivered and absorbed.

questions.prompt: A patient with hypoparathyroidism is experiencing muscle cramps and tetany. What is the nurse's first action?
options: Administer calcium supplements
Check parathyroid hormone levels
Encourage stretching exercises
Provide emotional support
questions.rationale: Hypoparathyroidism leads to low calcium levels, causing muscle cramps and tetany. Administering calcium supplements helps alleviate symptoms.

questions.prompt: The nurse is caring for a patient with a tracheostomy. Which of the following instructions should the nurse provide to the patient to prevent complications?
options: Limit fluid intake
Avoid humidified environments
Perform tracheostomy care daily
Encourage coughing and deep breathing
questions.rationale: Regular coughing and deep breathing exercises can help to clear secretions from the lungs and maintain a patent airway, reducing the risk of complications such as pneumonia.

questions.prompt: A 10-year-old child with a brain tumor is scared about an upcoming surgery. Which of the following is the most appropriate nursing action?
options: Reassure the child that everything will be okay
Explain the procedure in medical terms
Use simple, age-appropriate language to explain the procedure
Tell the child not to worry because the doctors are very good
questions.rationale: The best approach when communicating with a child is to use simple, age-appropriate language to explain procedures. This can help alleviate fears and anxiety. Options A and D may minimize the child's feelings, while option B may be too complex for a 10-year-old to understand.

questions.prompt: A nurse is caring for a patient who has a tracheostomy. Which of the following interventions would the nurse include in the plan of care to prevent a common complication associated with a tracheostomy?
options: Frequent oral care
Encourage ambulation
Turn the patient every 2 hours
Provide a high protein diet
questions.rationale: Frequent oral care helps to prevent infections, a common complication associated with a tracheostomy.

questions.prompt: A nurse is caring for a 12-year-old girl who has just been diagnosed with type 1 diabetes. Which of the following instructions should the nurse provide for self-care at home?
options: The child should avoid all forms of physical activity
The child should learn how to monitor her blood sugar levels
The child should restrict her fluid intake to prevent polyuria
The child should skip meals if she experiences hypoglycemia
questions.rationale: Correct answer: The child should learn how to monitor her blood sugar levels (Verified from PAEDIATRIC QUESTIONS.docx and Saunders 9th Ed.).

questions.prompt: A nurse is caring for a patient who suddenly becomes restless and anxious, with increased heart rate and decreased oxygen saturation. The nurse assesses decreased breath sounds on the right side of the chest. What should the nurse do next?
options: Administer a bronchodilator
Notify the physician immediately
Increase the rate of IV fluids
Position the patient on the left side
questions.rationale: These symptoms suggest a pneumothorax, a medical emergency. The nurse should notify the physician immediately for further intervention.

questions.prompt: A patient with cystic fibrosis has thick, tenacious secretions. Which medication would the nurse expect to administer to help the patient clear these secretions?
options: A corticosteroid
A mucolytic
An antihistamine
An antibiotic
questions.rationale: Mucolytic medications help to thin and loosen mucus in the airways, making it easier to cough up. This can be helpful for patients with cystic fibrosis, who often have thick, sticky mucus in their lungs.

questions.prompt: A patient with hyperthyroidism is experiencing exophthalmos. What is the nurse's first action?
options: Administer methylprednisolone
Check thyroid hormone levels
Encourage rest
Provide emotional support
questions.rationale: Methylprednisolone reduces inflammation and swelling.

questions.prompt: Which of the following symptoms should the nurse expect to find in a client diagnosed with right-sided heart failure?
options: Crackles in the lungs
Peripheral edema
Productive cough
Orthopnoea
questions.rationale: Right-sided heart failure results in systemic congestion, which manifests as peripheral edema. Crackles in the lungs, productive cough, and orthopnea are associated with left-sided heart failure due to pulmonary congestion.

questions.prompt: Question: A 2-year-old patient is suspected of having iron-deficiency anemia. Which symptom is most likely to be observed?
options: Frequent nosebleeds
Unexplained bruises
Rapid heart rate
Yellowing of the skin and eyes
questions.rationale: Correct answer: Rapid heart rate (Verified from PAEDIATRIC QUESTIONS.docx and Saunders 9th Ed.).

questions.prompt: A patient with a history of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) becomes confused and lethargic. The patient is breathing rapidly, and oxygen saturation is 86%. What should the nurse do first?
options: Administer supplemental oxygen
Encourage the patient to cough and deep breathe
Increase the IV fluid rate
Prepare to intubate the patient
questions.rationale: The patient's confusion, lethargy, tachypnea, and low oxygen saturation suggest hypoxemia. The nurse should administer supplemental oxygen to improve oxygenation.

questions.prompt: A nurse is caring for a patient with a chest tube connected to an underwater seal drainage system. Which of the following indicates a properly functioning system?
options: Constant bubbling in the water seal chamber
No fluctuations in the water seal chamber
Drainage system is kept at the level of the patient's chest
Fluctuations in the water seal chamber with respirations
questions.rationale: Normal functioning of an underwater seal drainage system is indicated by fluctuations (rising with inspiration and falling with expiration) in the water seal chamber with respirations.

questions.prompt: A patient with pneumonia has a decreased level of consciousness and is at risk for aspiration. Which of the following interventions would be most appropriate for this patient?
options: Place the patient in a supine position
Administer oxygen via nasal cannula
Use a spacer with metered-dose inhalers
Position the patient on their side
questions.rationale: A side-lying position can help prevent aspiration by allowing secretions to drain from the mouth. The other options would not specifically address the risk for aspiration in this patient.

questions.prompt: A 7-year-old child is newly diagnosed with Type 1 Diabetes Mellitus. The nurse would expect which of the following symptoms to have been present before diagnosis?
options: Weight gain
Bradycardia
Polydipsia
Hypertension
questions.rationale: Polydipsia (excessive thirst) is a classic symptom of Type 1 Diabetes Mellitus due to the body's inability to properly handle glucose, leading to high blood sugar levels and dehydration. Weight gain (option A) is more commonly associated with Type 2 Diabetes. Bradycardia (option B) and hypertension (option D) are not typical symptoms of Type 1 Diabetes.

questions.prompt: A patient who was recently in a car accident is having difficulty breathing. The nurse hears a grating sound during both inspiration and expiration. What could this indicate?
options: Normal lung sounds
Pneumothorax
Pleural effusion
Pleural friction rub
questions.rationale: Pleural friction rub is a grating sound produced when inflamed pleural surfaces rub together during respiration. This can occur in conditions such as pleuritis, which can result from trauma such as a car accident.

questions.prompt: A 2-year-old child presents with a "slapped cheek" appearance and a lacy rash on the body. What condition should the nurse suspect?
options: Measles
Roseola
Fifth disease
Scarlet fever
questions.rationale: Correct answer: Fifth disease (Verified from PAEDIATRIC QUESTIONS.docx and Saunders 9th Ed.).

questions.prompt: The charge nurse is delegating tasks for the day. Which of the following tasks can be delegated to a nursing assistant?
options: Administering medications
Performing sterile dressing changes
Assessing a patient's pain level
Assisting a patient with personal hygiene
questions.rationale: Correct answer: Assisting a patient with personal hygiene (Verified from eye and ear  QNS.docx and Saunders 9th Ed.).

questions.prompt: A 5-year-old child weighs 18 kg and is prescribed a medication at a dosage of 20 mg/kg/day in 2 divided doses. The medication comes in a concentration of 40 mg/2 mL. How many milliliters of medication will the nurse administer per dose?
options: 1 mL
2 mL
4.5 mL
9 mL
questions.rationale: Correct answer: 4.5 mL (Verified from PAEDIATRIC QUESTIONS.docx and Saunders 9th Ed.).

questions.prompt: A 4-year-old child weighing 40 pounds is prescribed acetaminophen at a dose of 15 mg/kg/dose every 4 hours. How many milligrams of acetaminophen will the nurse administer per dose?
options: 100 mg
200 mg
270 mg
300 mg
questions.rationale: Correct answer: 270 mg (Verified from PAEDIATRIC QUESTIONS.docx and Saunders 9th Ed.).

questions.prompt: A 6-month-old infant weighing 7 kg is ordered an antibiotic medication at a dose of 10 mg/kg/day divided into 2 doses. How many milligrams of medication will the nurse administer for each dose?
options: 10 mg
20 mg
35 mg
50 mg
questions.rationale: Correct answer: 35 mg (Verified from PAEDIATRIC QUESTIONS.docx and Saunders 9th Ed.).

questions.prompt: A patient with diabetes is experiencing symptoms of gastroparesis. What is the nurse's first action?
options: Administer metoclopramide
Check blood glucose levels
Encourage fluid intake
Provide nutritional support
questions.rationale: Metoclopramide enhances gastric motility.

questions.prompt: A client with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) is experiencing shortness of breath. What position should the nurse instruct the patient to assume to facilitate breathing?
options: Supine
Prone
High Fowler's
Trendelenburg
questions.rationale: The High Fowler's position, sitting up at 90 degrees, allows for maximum lung expansion and can help improve oxygenation in a patient with COPD.

questions.prompt: A patient with hyperparathyroidism is experiencing bone pain. What is the primary goal of treatment?
options: Decrease calcium levels
Increase calcium levels
Regulate bone metabolism
Reduce kidney stone formation
questions.rationale: Lowering calcium levels alleviates bone pain.

questions.prompt: A 2-year-old child has been prescribed a liquid medication. The prescription calls for 5 mL to be given twice daily. The parents are unsure how to measure this amount. What should the nurse recommend?
options: Use a teaspoon from the kitchen.
Use the dropper that came with the medication.
Use a measuring cup.
Use a syringe without a needle.
questions.rationale: Correct answer: Use a syringe without a needle. (Verified from pediatric problems continued.pptx and Saunders 9th Ed.).

blocks.title: Pediatric Emergencies, Congenital Defects & Growth Milestones
rows: **Epiglottitis vs. Croup**
**Epiglottitis:** Tripod posture, drooling, dysphagia, high fever. **Croup:** Barking seal cough, stridor.
**Epiglottitis: NEVER examine throat with tongue blade** (airway spasm!) — keep calm + prep intubation.
**Pyloric Stenosis vs. Intussusception**
**Pyloric:** Olive-shaped RUQ mass, projectile non-bilious vomiting. **Intussusception:** **Currant-jelly stools**, sausage mass.
Correct dehydration/electrolytes before pyloromyotomy; air/hydrostatic enema for intussusception.
**Tetralogy of Fallot (Tet Spells)**
Acute cyanosis, irritability, hypoxia during crying/feeding.
Place infant immediately in **knee-to-chest position**, give O2 & morphine.
**Pediatric Milestones & Meds**
2 mo: social smile; 6 mo: sits w/ support; 12 mo: 3x birth weight; 24 mo: 2-word phrases.
Measure oral liquids with **oral syringe** (never kitchen spoon); calculate **safe mg/kg/day**.

quiz.prompt: A 2-month-old infant is brought to the clinic for a well-baby check-up. Which of the following developmental milestones would the nurse expect to observe?
options: Sitting without support
Rolling over from back to stomach

"It is fine to take over-the-counter NSAIDs alongside my prescribed anticoagulants without asking."
questions.rationale: Effective client education in Croup, Epiglottitis, RSV, Cystic Fibrosis & Congenital Heart Defects requires adherence to therapy, scheduled lab follow-ups, and prompt reporting of acute deterioration.

questions.prompt: A 4-year-old child weighing 40 pounds is prescribed acetaminophen at a dose of 15 mg/kg/dose every 4 hours. How many milligrams of acetaminophen will the nurse administer per dose?
options: 100 mg
200 mg
270 mg
300 mg
questions.rationale: Correct answer: 270 mg (Verified from PAEDIATRIC QUESTIONS.docx and Saunders 9th Ed.).

questions.prompt: A 2-month-old infant is brought to the clinic for a well-baby check-up. Which of the following developmental milestones would the nurse expect to observe?
options: Sitting without support
Rolling over from back to stomach
Smiling in response to familiar faces
Walking with support
questions.rationale: Correct answer: Smiling in response to familiar faces (Verified from PAEDIATRIC QUESTIONS.docx and Saunders 9th Ed.).

questions.prompt: A 5-year-old child weighs 18 kg and is prescribed a medication at a dosage of 20 mg/kg/day in 2 divided doses. The medication comes in a concentration of 40 mg/2 mL. How many milliliters of medication will the nurse administer per dose?
options: 1 mL
2 mL
4.5 mL
9 mL
questions.rationale: Correct answer: 4.5 mL (Verified from PAEDIATRIC QUESTIONS.docx and Saunders 9th Ed.).

questions.prompt: A 1-year-old child weighing 10 kg is ordered amoxicillin at a dose of 25 mg/kg/day in 2 divided doses. How many milligrams of amoxicillin will the nurse administer for each dose?
options: 50 mg
75 mg
100 mg
125 mg
questions.rationale: Correct answer: 125 mg (Verified from PAEDIATRIC QUESTIONS.docx and Saunders 9th Ed.).

questions.prompt: Which client care task related to Pyloric Stenosis, Intussusception, Rheumatic Fever & Pediatric mg/kg is appropriate to delegate to an Unlicensed Assistive Personnel (UAP)?
options: Providing initial discharge teaching on red-flag warning signs.
Evaluating the client's therapeutic response to an intravenous high-alert medication.
Obtaining routine vital signs and strictly measuring oral intake and urine output on a stable client.
Performing the comprehensive admission assessment for a newly arrived acute client.
questions.rationale: Per LaCharity PDA and NCSBN delegation rules, UAPs perform routine, stable data collection (vitals, I&O, ADLs), while assessment, teaching, and evaluation remain RN-only duties.

questions.prompt: A nurse cares for a client presenting with Epiglottitis vs. Croup (Pyloric Stenosis, Intussusception, Rheumatic Fever & Pediatric mg/kg). What is the priority nursing action?
options: Wait 4 hours to reassess before taking any action or documenting.
Administer sedatives or diuretics without reviewing baseline labs or vitals.
Epiglottitis: Tripod posture, drooling, dysphagia, high fever. Croup: Barking seal cough, stridor.
Delegate acute clinical assessment and teaching to UAP/CNA.
questions.rationale: For Epiglottitis vs. Croup, the priority intervention is: Epiglottitis: Tripod posture, drooling, dysphagia, high fever. Croup: Barking seal cough, stridor. Key exam watchpoint: Epiglottitis: NEVER examine throat with tongue blade (airway spasm!) — keep calm + prep intubation.

questions.prompt: A 6-year-old child weighing 20 kg is scheduled to receive a dose of medication. The medication is ordered at a dose of 5 mg/kg/dose every 8 hours. The medication comes in a concentration of 100 mg/5 mL. How many milliliters of medication will the nurse administer per dose?
options: 1 mL
2 mL
3 mL
5 mL
questions.rationale: Correct answer: 2 mL (Verified from PAEDIATRIC QUESTIONS.docx and Saunders 9th Ed.).

questions.prompt: A 3-year-old child weighing 15 kg is prescribed a medication at a dose of 50 mg/kg/day in 4 divided doses. How many milligrams of the medication will the nurse administer per dose?
options: 75 mg
100 mg
200 mg
questions.rationale: Correct answer: 187.5 mg (Verified from PAEDIATRIC QUESTIONS.docx and Saunders 9th Ed.).

questions.prompt: A 12-year-old child weighing 50 kg is ordered a medication at a dose of 5 mg/kg/day in 3 divided doses. How many milligrams of the medication will the nurse administer per dose?
options: 30 mg
50 mg
75 mg
83 mg
questions.rationale: Correct answer: 83 mg (Verified from PAEDIATRIC QUESTIONS.docx and Saunders 9th Ed.).

questions.prompt: A nurse is caring for a client who has a tracheostomy. Which of the following interventions should the nurse include in the plan of care?
options: Provide tracheostomy care every shift
Use sterile technique when suctioning the tracheostomy
Encourage the client to cough and deep breathe every 2 hours
All of the above
questions.rationale: All the listed interventions are part of the appropriate care for a client with a tracheostomy. They all help maintain a patent airway, promote effective gas exchange, and prevent infection.

questions.prompt: A nurse is preparing to administer albuterol to a patient with asthma. Which of the following should the nurse monitor for as a potential side effect of this medication?
options: Bradycardia
Hypotension
Tachycardia
Hypoglycaemia
questions.rationale: Albuterol, a beta2-adrenergic agonist, can cause tachycardia as a side effect. It stimulates the beta2 receptors in the lungs causing bronchodilation, but it can also stimulate beta1 receptors in the heart causing increased heart rate.

questions.prompt: A patient with diabetes is experiencing symptoms of gastroparesis. What is the nurse's first action?
options: Administer metoclopramide
Check blood glucose levels
Encourage fluid intake
Provide nutritional support
questions.rationale: Metoclopramide enhances gastric motility.

questions.prompt: A patient with Cushing's syndrome is experiencing weight gain and hypertension. What is the primary goal of treatment?
options: Decrease cortisol production
Increase cortisol production
Regulate blood pressure
Reduce weight
questions.rationale: Reducing cortisol levels manages symptoms.

questions.prompt: A patient on a ventilator is experiencing a decrease in oxygen saturation. The nurse increases the fraction of inspired oxygen (FiO2) but the saturation does not improve. What should the nurse do next?
options: Increase the respiratory rate on the ventilator
Administer a bronchodilator
Perform endotracheal suctioning
Increase the positive end-expiratory pressure (PEEP)
questions.rationale: The nurse should next perform endotracheal suctioning to clear any secretions that might be obstructing the airway and affecting oxygenation. If this does not improve oxygenation, other interventions such as increasing PEEP may be considered.

questions.prompt: A patient with asthma has a peak flow reading that is 50% of their personal best. Which of the following actions should the nurse take?
options: Encourage the patient to rest and continue monitoring
Administer a bronchodilator
Increase the oxygen flow rate
Prepare for endotracheal intubation
questions.rationale: A peak flow reading that is 50% of the personal best indicates a severe decrease in lung function. The nurse should administer a bronchodilator to help open the airways and improve breathing.

questions.prompt: A patient with a history of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) becomes confused and lethargic. The patient is breathing rapidly, and oxygen saturation is 86%. What should the nurse do first?
options: Administer supplemental oxygen
Encourage the patient to cough and deep breathe
Increase the IV fluid rate
Prepare to intubate the patient
questions.rationale: The patient's confusion, lethargy, tachypnea, and low oxygen saturation suggest hypoxemia. The nurse should administer supplemental oxygen to improve oxygenation.

questions.prompt: A patient with hypothyroidism is experiencing depression. What is the nurse's first action?
options: Increase levothyroxine dose
Check thyroid-stimulating hormone (TSH) levels
Encourage exercise
Provide emotional support
questions.rationale: TSH level assessment guides levothyroxine dose adjustments.

questions.prompt: A patient with hyperparathyroidism is experiencing kidney stones. What is the primary goal of treatment?
options: Decrease calcium levels
Increase calcium levels
Regulate bone metabolism
Reduce kidney stone formation
questions.rationale: Lowering calcium levels reduces kidney stone formation risk.

questions.prompt: A nurse is assessing a patient who may have a perforated eardrum. Which of the following symptoms would likely be present?
options: Ringing in the ears
Ear pain that suddenly stops
Hearing loss
All of the above
questions.rationale: A perforated eardrum can cause ringing in the ears (tinnitus), sudden cessation of ear pain (as the pressure is relieved by the perforation), and hearing loss. Therefore, all of these symptoms might be present if a patient has a perforated eardrum.

questions.prompt: A patient with hypothyroidism is taking levothyroxine. What is the primary goal of treatment?
options: Increase thyroid hormone production
Decrease thyroid hormone production
Regulate metabolism
Reduce weight
questions.rationale: Levothyroxine replaces deficient thyroid hormones.

questions.prompt: A nurse is prioritizing care for a patient who has been newly diagnosed with Meniere's disease. Which of the following should be the nurse's first action?
options: Providing patient education about the disease
Starting the patient on a low-sodium diet
Administering prescribed medication
Assessing the patient's current level of knowledge
questions.rationale: Correct answer: Assessing the patient's current level of knowledge (Verified from eye and ear  QNS.docx and Saunders 9th Ed.).

questions.prompt: A patient with type 1 diabetes is experiencing diabetic retinopathy. What is the nurse's primary goal?
options: Improve vision
Reduce blood glucose levels
Increase insulin production
Enhance renal function
questions.rationale: Controlling blood glucose levels slows retinopathy progression.

questions.prompt: A 10-year-old child is undergoing radiation therapy for a brain tumour. Which of the following side effects is the child most likely to experience?
options: Hair loss
Hearing loss
Vision loss
Weight loss
questions.rationale: While radiation therapy can potentially cause all these side effects, hair loss is the most common and immediate side effect of radiation therapy to the brain.

questions.prompt: A 5-year-old child is admitted with suspected appendicitis. Which symptom is the nurse likely to find?
options: Diarrhea
Right lower quadrant pain
Left upper quadrant pain
Constipation
questions.rationale: The most common symptom of appendicitis is abdominal pain that begins near the belly button and then shifts to the lower right side of the abdomen. Diarrhea (option A) and constipation (option D) can occur but are not as specific. Left upper quadrant pain (option C) is not typically associated with appendicitis.

questions.prompt: A patient with acromegaly is taking octreotide. What is the primary goal of treatment?
options: Decrease growth hormone production
Increase growth hormone production
Regulate metabolism
Reduce tumor size
questions.rationale: Octreotide inhibits growth hormone release, helping to manage acromegaly symptoms.

questions.prompt: A patient is admitted with a diagnosis of pulmonary embolism. What is the priority nursing intervention for this patient?
options: Administer anticoagulants as ordered
Encourage ambulation
Provide supplemental oxygen
Monitor vital signs
questions.rationale: The immediate priority for a patient with a pulmonary embolism is to improve oxygenation, which can be achieved by providing supplemental oxygen.

questions.prompt: A nurse is caring for a patient with an underwater seal chest drainage system. What should the nurse do if the chest tube becomes disconnected from the system?
options: Clamp the chest tube immediately
Place the end of the chest tube in a container of sterile saline
Apply an occlusive dressing over the chest tube site
Reconnect the chest tube to the drainage system as quickly as possible
questions.rationale: If a chest tube becomes disconnected, the nurse should immediately place the end of the tube in a container of sterile saline to maintain a water seal and prevent air from entering the pleural space.

questions.prompt: A 7-year-old child is newly diagnosed with Type 1 Diabetes Mellitus. The nurse would expect which of the following symptoms to have been present before diagnosis?
options: Weight gain
Bradycardia
Polydipsia
Hypertension
questions.rationale: Polydipsia (excessive thirst) is a classic symptom of Type 1 Diabetes Mellitus due to the body's inability to properly handle glucose, leading to high blood sugar levels and dehydration. Weight gain (option A) is more commonly associated with Type 2 Diabetes. Bradycardia (option B) and hypertension (option D) are not typical symptoms of Type 1 Diabetes.

items: Principles 1. Communication includes verbal and nonverbal expression 2. Successful communication includes appropriateness, efficiency, flexibility, and feedback.

options: Delegate acute clinical assessment and teaching to UAP/CNA.
Wait 4 hours to reassess before taking any action or documenting.
Administer sedatives or diuretics without reviewing baseline labs or vitals.
High fever, severe 'lead-pipe' rigidity, tachycardia, high CPK.

quiz.prompt: A client managed for Therapeutic Communication, Suicide Risk, Abuse & Crisis Intervention develops sudden tachypnea (RR 32/min), SpO2 87%, and new-onset restlessness. What should the nurse do FIRST?
options: Ask the UAP to assist the client to ambulate in the hallway.
Elevate the head of the bed, assess airway/lung sounds, and apply supplemental oxygen.
Document the vital signs and recheck oxygen saturation in 2 hours.
Administer a PRN opioid analgesic for restlessness before assessing.
quiz.rationale: Under Maslow's hierarchy and ABC prioritization in Therapeutic Communication, Suicide Risk, Abuse & Crisis Intervention, airway and oxygenation cues (SpO2 87%, RR 32, hypoxia-induced restlessness) require immediate airway/O2 support first.

quiz.prompt: Which client care task related to Therapeutic Communication, Suicide Risk, Abuse & Crisis Intervention is appropriate to delegate to an Unlicensed Assistive Personnel (UAP)?

Obtaining routine vital signs and strictly measuring oral intake and urine output on a stable client.
quiz.rationale: Per LaCharity PDA and NCSBN delegation rules, UAPs perform routine, stable data collection (vitals, I&O, ADLs), while assessment, teaching, and evaluation remain RN-only duties.

quiz.prompt: A preceptor reviews discharge teaching for a client recovering under Therapeutic Communication, Suicide Risk, Abuse & Crisis Intervention. Which statement by the client indicates teaching was effective?

"I will monitor for warning signs like fever, worsening shortness of breath, or bleeding and contact my provider promptly."
"It is fine to take over-the-counter NSAIDs alongside my prescribed anticoagulants without asking."

quiz.rationale: Effective client education in Therapeutic Communication, Suicide Risk, Abuse & Crisis Intervention requires adherence to therapy, scheduled lab follow-ups, and prompt reporting of acute deterioration.

quiz.prompt: When using the NCSBN 6-Step Clinical Judgment Model (CJMM) for a client in Course Unit 16: Psychiatric Mental Health, Crisis Care & Psychotherapeutic Medications, what directly follows 'Recognize Cues' and 'Analyze Cues'?
options: Delegate hypothesis ranking to support staff before completing assessment.
Prioritize Hypotheses — ranking immediate life-threatening complications first.
Evaluate Outcomes prior to implementing any bedside intervention.
Archive the admission chart without creating a care plan.
quiz.rationale: The 6 steps of the NCSBN CJMM progress in order: Recognize Cues -> Analyze Cues -> Prioritize Hypotheses -> Generate Solutions -> Take Action -> Evaluate Outcomes.

quiz.prompt: A patient is experiencing vertigo. The nurse knows that this symptom is likely related to a problem with what part of the sensory system?
options: Visual system
Vestibular system
Olfactory system
Tactile system
quiz.rationale: The vestibular system (B), located within the inner ear, is responsible for maintaining balance and spatial orientation. Vertigo, a sensation of feeling off balance, is often caused by problems in this system. The visual (A), olfactory (C), and tactile (D) systems are not typically associated with symptoms of vertigo.

quiz.prompt: As a nurse leader, you notice that one of your team members is consistently late for their shift. What is the most appropriate action?
options: Ignore the behavior as it doesn't affect patient care.
Report the behavior to the hospital administration.
Discuss the issue with the team member privately.
Publicly reprimand the team member during a staff meeting.
quiz.rationale: In this situation, the most appropriate action for a nurse leader is to address the issue directly with the individual involved (C). Ignoring the behavior (A) is not an effective leadership strategy as it fails to address the issue. Reporting the behavior to administration (B) should be a last resort if the behavior continues after addressing it directly. Publicly reprimanding the team member (D) is not appropriate and could create a hostile work environment.

quiz.prompt: As a nurse leader, you are implementing a change in a hospital protocol. What is the best way to ensure staff compliance with this change?
options: Enforce strict punishments for non-compliance.
Communicate the rationale for the change.
Make the change without explaining why.
Implement the change without seeking staff input.
quiz.rationale: Effective leadership involves open and clear communication. Explaining the rationale for the change (B) helps staff understand the importance and necessity of the change, thereby fostering compliance. Enforcing strict punishments (A) tends to create a negative work environment. Implementing a change without explanation (C) or without seeking staff input (D) can lead to resistance and non-compliance.

quiz.prompt: A nurse is teaching a patient who has been diagnosed with glaucoma. Which of the following statements by the patient indicates the need for further teaching?

Democratic
Transactional
quiz.rationale: Correct answer: Democratic (Verified from eye and ear  QNS.docx and Saunders 9th Ed.).

quiz.prompt: A nurse is assessing a patient with suspected macular degeneration. Which of the following findings would most likely indicate this condition?

Central vision loss
quiz.rationale: Correct answer: Central vision loss (Verified from eye and ear  QNS.docx and Saunders 9th Ed.).

quiz.prompt: As a nurse leader, you observe a conflict between two team members. What is the most appropriate initial action?
options: Ignore the conflict and hope it resolves itself.
Immediately report the incident to higher management.
Facilitate a meeting between the two individuals to discuss the issue.
Take sides with the person who has been with the team longer.
quiz.rationale: Correct answer: Facilitate a meeting between the two individuals to discuss the issue. (Verified from eye and ear  QNS.docx and Saunders 9th Ed.).

quiz.prompt: A patient with diabetes reports experiencing numbness and tingling in their feet. This is most likely indicative of which of the following conditions?

Diabetic neuropathy
Diabetic nephropathy
Diabetic ketoacidosis
quiz.rationale: Correct answer: Diabetic neuropathy (Verified from eye and ear  QNS.docx and Saunders 9th Ed.).

quiz.prompt: A patient with a history of glaucoma has been prescribed eye drops to decrease intraocular pressure. The patient also has other chronic conditions that require medication. Which of the following should be the nurse's priority instruction?
options: "Take your glaucoma eye drops first before any other medication."

"Take your glaucoma eye drops last after all other medications."

quiz.rationale: Correct answer: "Take your glaucoma eye drops first before any other medication." (Verified from eye and ear  QNS.docx and Saunders 9th Ed.).

quiz.prompt: A nurse is prioritizing care for a patient who has been newly diagnosed with Meniere's disease. Which of the following should be the nurse's first action?
options: Providing patient education about the disease
Starting the patient on a low-sodium diet
Administering prescribed medication
Assessing the patient's current level of knowledge
quiz.rationale: Correct answer: Assessing the patient's current level of knowledge (Verified from eye and ear  QNS.docx and Saunders 9th Ed.).

quiz.prompt: A patient with a spinal cord injury report experiencing phantom limb pain. The nurse should prioritize which of the following interventions?
options: Administering prescribed pain medication
Reassuring the patient that the pain is not real
Teaching the patient distraction techniques
Assessing the patient's pain level and characteristics
quiz.rationale: Correct answer: Assessing the patient's pain level and characteristics (Verified from eye and ear  QNS.docx and Saunders 9th Ed.).

blocks.text: **Depression, Bipolar Mania, Schizophrenia, Eating & Substance Disorders** is a high-yield focus area in **Course Unit 16: Psychiatric Mental Health, Crisis Care & Psychotherapeutic Medications** for the Next-Generation NCLEX-RN (NGN). This study guide integrates core pathophysiology, clinical judgment cues, pharmacology safety, and bedside nursing priorities across **Saunders Comprehensive Review (9th Ed.)**, **Kaplan NCLEX-RN Prep**, and **LaCharity PDA**.

items: Bipolar disorder is characterized by extreme changes in mood, energy, and the ability to function.
The classifications include bipolar I disorder, bipolar II disorder, cyclothymic disorder, and mixed features.

Bipolar I disorder: Most severe form, characterized by severe mood episodes from mania to depression Bipolar II disorder: A milder form of mood elevation; there are milder episodes of hypomania that alternate with periods of severe depression.
Depression affects feelings, thoughts, and behaviors. Depression is one of the most common psychiatric disorders.
Hygiene Care Monitor for general hygiene and self-care deficits; may indicate worsening depression.

Schizophrenia is a group of mental health problems characterized by psychotic features (hallucinations and delusions), disordered thought processes, and disrupted interpersonal relationships. Disturbances in affect, mood, behavior, and thought processes occur.
Intervention for Schizophrenia Maintain a safe environment.

Typical antipsychotics are more effective for positive symptoms of schizophrenia, such as hallucinations, aggression, and delusions; these medications also block the chemoreceptor trigger zone and vomiting center in the brain, producing an antiemetic effect.
Atypical antipsychotics are more effective for the negative symptoms of schizophrenia, such as avolition, apathy, and alogia.
Benzodiazepines -Medications include chlordiazepoxide, clorazepate, diazepam, lorazepam, and oxazepam. These are the most effective medications to facilitate alcohol withdrawal.

items: Intervention for Schizophrenia Maintain a safe environment.

Typical antipsychotics are more effective for positive symptoms of schizophrenia, such as hallucinations, aggression, and delusions; these medications also block the chemoreceptor trigger zone and vomiting center in the brain, producing an antiemetic effect.
Atypical antipsychotics are more effective for the negative symptoms of schizophrenia, such as avolition, apathy, and alogia.
Benzodiazepines -Medications include chlordiazepoxide, clorazepate, diazepam, lorazepam, and oxazepam. These are the most effective medications to facilitate alcohol withdrawal.

Central alpha-adrenergic agonist-Medications include clonidine. Used to decrease the autonomic component of withdrawal symptoms Maintaining Abstinence -Medications can be prescribed to clients to help maintain abstinence.
Clonidine -Used to decrease the autonomic component of withdrawal symptoms .Side effects include fatigue, dizziness, irritability, and dry mouth.
Galantamine An inhibitor of cholinesterase used to treat mild to moderate dementia of Alzheimer’s disease Side and adverse effects include nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, anorexia, and weight loss.

items: Risk factors include genetic predisposition, dysregulation of serotonin and/or norepinephrine, inflammatory processes, stressful or traumatic life events, and various psychological factors.
Inhibit serotonin uptake and elicit an antidepressant response.

Serotonin-norepinephrine reuptake inhibitors (SNRI) are similar to SSRIs, but they also work by blocking the effects of norepinephrine in addition to serotonin. Considerations are similar to that of SSRIs.

The therapeutic medication serum level of lithium is 0.6 to 1.2 mEq/L (0.6 to 1.2 mmol/L); the actual dose at which the therapeutic effect is achieved and the levels at which toxicity occurs are highly variable among individual clients.
Lithium Toxicity Occurs when ingested lithium cannot be detoxified and excreted by the kidneys b. Symptoms of toxicity begin to appear when the serum lithium level is at 1.5 mEq/L (1.5 mmol/L).
Symptoms vary from mild, moderate and severe toxicity Interventions for lithium toxicity Withhold lithium and notify the PHCP.
Prepare to obtain samples to monitor lithium, electrolytes, blood urea nitrogen, and creatinine levels and perform a complete blood cell count.

Delegate acute clinical assessment and teaching to UAP/CNA.
Administer sedatives or diuretics without reviewing baseline labs or vitals.

questions.prompt: A preceptor reviews discharge teaching for a client recovering under Depression, Bipolar Mania, Schizophrenia, Eating & Substance Disorders. Which statement by the client indicates teaching was effective?
options: "I will monitor for warning signs like fever, worsening shortness of breath, or bleeding and contact my provider promptly."

questions.prompt: As a nurse leader, you notice that one of your team members is consistently late for their shift. What is the most appropriate action?
options: Ignore the behavior as it doesn't affect patient care.
Report the behavior to the hospital administration.
Discuss the issue with the team member privately.
Publicly reprimand the team member during a staff meeting.
questions.rationale: In this situation, the most appropriate action for a nurse leader is to address the issue directly with the individual involved (C). Ignoring the behavior (A) is not an effective leadership strategy as it fails to address the issue. Reporting the behavior to administration (B) should be a last resort if the behavior continues after addressing it directly. Publicly reprimanding the team member (D) is not appropriate and could create a hostile work environment.

questions.prompt: A nurse is assessing a patient with suspected macular degeneration. Which of the following findings would most likely indicate this condition?

Difficulty distinguishing colors
Blurred vision
Central vision loss
questions.rationale: Correct answer: Central vision loss (Verified from eye and ear  QNS.docx and Saunders 9th Ed.).

questions.prompt: A patient with a spinal cord injury report experiencing phantom limb pain. The nurse should prioritize which of the following interventions?
options: Administering prescribed pain medication
Reassuring the patient that the pain is not real
Teaching the patient distraction techniques
Assessing the patient's pain level and characteristics
questions.rationale: Correct answer: Assessing the patient's pain level and characteristics (Verified from eye and ear  QNS.docx and Saunders 9th Ed.).

questions.prompt: A client managed for Therapeutic Communication, Suicide Risk, Abuse & Crisis Intervention develops sudden tachypnea (RR 32/min), SpO2 87%, and new-onset restlessness. What should the nurse do FIRST?

Elevate the head of the bed, assess airway/lung sounds, and apply supplemental oxygen.
Document the vital signs and recheck oxygen saturation in 2 hours.
Administer a PRN opioid analgesic for restlessness before assessing.

questions.prompt: Which statement reflects an unsafe error (or NCLEX trap) that the nurse must AVOID when managing Lithium?
options: Therapeutic 0.6–1.2 mEq/L (>1.5 toxic); low Na+ or dehydration increases toxicity!
Maintain normal sodium & hydration; report coarse tremor, ataxia, severe diarrhea, confusion.
Use closed-loop SBAR communication when escalating abnormal clinical changes.
Monitor vital signs, airway, and target labs closely during care of Lithium.
questions.rationale: When caring for Lithium, avoiding this unsafe action is critical: Maintain normal sodium & hydration; report coarse tremor, ataxia, severe diarrhea, confusion.

questions.prompt: A patient is experiencing vertigo. The nurse knows that this symptom is likely related to a problem with what part of the sensory system?
options: Visual system
Vestibular system
Olfactory system
Tactile system
questions.rationale: The vestibular system (B), located within the inner ear, is responsible for maintaining balance and spatial orientation. Vertigo, a sensation of feeling off balance, is often caused by problems in this system. The visual (A), olfactory (C), and tactile (D) systems are not typically associated with symptoms of vertigo.

questions.prompt: A nurse is prioritizing care for a patient who has been newly diagnosed with Meniere's disease. Which of the following should be the nurse's first action?
options: Providing patient education about the disease
Starting the patient on a low-sodium diet
Administering prescribed medication
Assessing the patient's current level of knowledge
questions.rationale: Correct answer: Assessing the patient's current level of knowledge (Verified from eye and ear  QNS.docx and Saunders 9th Ed.).

questions.prompt: A patient with diabetes reports experiencing numbness and tingling in their feet. This is most likely indicative of which of the following conditions?
options: Diabetic retinopathy
Diabetic neuropathy
Diabetic nephropathy
Diabetic ketoacidosis
questions.rationale: Correct answer: Diabetic neuropathy (Verified from eye and ear  QNS.docx and Saunders 9th Ed.).

questions.prompt: A nurse is teaching a patient who has been diagnosed with glaucoma. Which of the following statements by the patient indicates the need for further teaching?
options: "I will need to use my eye drops daily."
"I will avoid straining during bowel movements."
"I am glad I can stop taking my eye drops once my symptoms improve."
"I understand that I will need regular check-ups for my eye pressure."
questions.rationale: Correct answer: "I am glad I can stop taking my eye drops once my symptoms improve." (Verified from eye and ear  QNS.docx and Saunders 9th Ed.).

questions.prompt: A nurse cares for a client presenting with Alcohol Withdrawal (DTs) (Therapeutic Communication, Suicide Risk, Abuse & Crisis Intervention). What is the priority nursing action?

Tremors, hallucinations, autonomic hyperactivity (48–72 hrs post-stop).

Prioritize Hypotheses — ranking immediate life-threatening complications first.
Evaluate Outcomes prior to implementing any bedside intervention.
Archive the admission chart without creating a care plan.
questions.rationale: The 6 steps of the NCSBN CJMM progress in order: Recognize Cues -> Analyze Cues -> Prioritize Hypotheses -> Generate Solutions -> Take Action -> Evaluate Outcomes.

questions.prompt: A patient with a history of glaucoma has been prescribed eye drops to decrease intraocular pressure. The patient also has other chronic conditions that require medication. Which of the following should be the nurse's priority instruction?

"You can take your glaucoma eye drops at the same time as your other medications."
"Take your glaucoma eye drops last after all other medications."
"The timing of your glaucoma eye drops in relation to other medications doesn't matter."

Take sides with the person who has been with the team longer.

questions.prompt: As a nurse leader, you are implementing a change in a hospital protocol. What is the best way to ensure staff compliance with this change?

Make the change without explaining why.
Implement the change without seeking staff input.

Enforcing strict punishments (A) tends to create a negative work environment. Implementing a change without explanation (C) or without seeking staff input (D) can lead to resistance and non-compliance.

questions.prompt: A 7-year-old child is newly diagnosed with Type 1 Diabetes Mellitus. The nurse would expect which of the following symptoms to have been present before diagnosis?
options: Weight gain
Bradycardia
Polydipsia
Hypertension
questions.rationale: Polydipsia (excessive thirst) is a classic symptom of Type 1 Diabetes Mellitus due to the body's inability to properly handle glucose, leading to high blood sugar levels and dehydration. Weight gain (option A) is more commonly associated with Type 2 Diabetes. Bradycardia (option B) and hypertension (option D) are not typical symptoms of Type 1 Diabetes.

questions.prompt: A nurse is caring for a patient with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) who is receiving oxygen therapy. A family member asks the nurse why the patient isn't receiving a higher flow of oxygen. What should the nurse explain?
options: The patient's oxygen levels are within the normal range
High levels of oxygen can suppress the patient's drive to breathe
The patient is comfortable and not experiencing any distress
The doctor has not ordered an increase in oxygen
questions.rationale: Patients with COPD often rely on a low oxygen level to stimulate their breathing. Providing too much oxygen can reduce their respiratory drive and lead to respiratory depression.

questions.prompt: A patient with cystic fibrosis has thick, tenacious secretions. Which medication would the nurse expect to administer to help the patient clear these secretions?
options: A corticosteroid
A mucolytic
An antihistamine
An antibiotic
questions.rationale: Mucolytic medications help to thin and loosen mucus in the airways, making it easier to cough up. This can be helpful for patients with cystic fibrosis, who often have thick, sticky mucus in their lungs.

questions.prompt: The RN is delegating tasks to a licensed practical nurse (LPN). Which of the following tasks is appropriate for the RN to delegate to the LPN?
options: Developing a nursing care plan
Performing an initial patient assessment
Administering IV push medications
Monitoring a patient's response to medications
questions.rationale: Correct answer: Monitoring a patient's response to medications (Verified from eye and ear  QNS.docx and Saunders 9th Ed.).

questions.prompt: A nurse is providing dietary education to the parents of a child with celiac disease. Which food should the nurse instruct the parents to eliminate from the child's diet?
options: Rice
Wheat
Corn
Potatoes
questions.rationale: Celiac disease is a disorder where ingestion of gluten leads to damage in the small intestine. Gluten is found in wheat, rye, and barley. Therefore, wheat should be eliminated from the diet of a child with celiac disease. Rice (option A), corn (option C), and potatoes (option D) are naturally gluten-free and can be included in the diet.

questions.prompt: A nurse is delegating tasks to a nursing assistant for a patient with pneumonia. Which of the following tasks can the nurse safely delegate?
options: Auscultation of lung sounds
Encouraging fluid intake
Administering antibiotics
Evaluating the patient's response to treatment
questions.rationale: Encouraging fluid intake can be safely delegated to a nursing assistant. The other tasks require nursing judgement and should be performed by the nurse.

questions.prompt: A nurse is caring for a 3-year-old child with celiac disease. Which dietary instruction is most appropriate?
options: The child should avoid foods containing gluten.
The child should follow a low-protein diet.
The child should consume a high-fat diet.
The child should increase intake of dairy products.
questions.rationale: Celiac disease is an autoimmune disorder where ingestion of gluten leads to damage in the small intestine. Avoiding gluten is the primary treatment. Options B, C, and D are not typically recommended for children with celiac disease.

questions.prompt: A patient with acromegaly is taking octreotide. What is the primary goal of treatment?
options: Decrease growth hormone production
Increase growth hormone production
Regulate metabolism
Reduce tumor size
questions.rationale: Octreotide inhibits growth hormone release, helping to manage acromegaly symptoms.

questions.prompt: A nurse is caring for a patient with a respiratory rate of 6 breaths per minute. The patient is lethargic and unresponsive. Which of the following actions should the nurse take?
options: Administer oxygen
Position the patient on their side
Prepare for intubation
Initiate CPR
questions.rationale: A respiratory rate of 6 breaths per minute is dangerously low and indicates respiratory failure. The patient is unresponsive, suggesting a lack of oxygen to the brain. Immediate intervention, such as intubation, is needed.

questions.prompt: A patient with asthma has a peak flow reading that is 50% of their personal best. Which of the following actions should the nurse take?
options: Encourage the patient to rest and continue monitoring
Administer a bronchodilator
Increase the oxygen flow rate
Prepare for endotracheal intubation
questions.rationale: A peak flow reading that is 50% of the personal best indicates a severe decrease in lung function. The nurse should administer a bronchodilator to help open the airways and improve breathing.

questions.prompt: A patient with pheochromocytoma is experiencing hypertension and tachycardia. What is the nurse's first action?
options: Administer alpha blockers
Check catecholamine levels
Encourage relaxation techniques
Provide oxygen therapy
questions.rationale: Alpha blockers help control blood pressure and reduce symptoms.

questions.prompt: A nurse is providing care for a patient who has a new tracheostomy. What is the priority nursing action?
options: Encourage the patient to speak
Maintain a patent airway
Provide emotional support
Assist with personal hygiene
questions.rationale: Maintaining a patent airway is a priority for a patient with a tracheostomy. The nurse should frequently assess the tracheostomy tube and the surrounding area for patency and signs of infection.

questions.prompt: A client with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) is experiencing shortness of breath. What position should the nurse instruct the patient to assume to facilitate breathing?
options: Supine
Prone
High Fowler's
Trendelenburg
questions.rationale: The High Fowler's position, sitting up at 90 degrees, allows for maximum lung expansion and can help improve oxygenation in a patient with COPD.

questions.prompt: A patient with multiple endocrine neoplasia (MEN) is experiencing symptoms of medullary thyroid cancer. What is the primary goal of treatment?
options: Decrease calcium levels
Increase calcium levels
Regulate bone metabolism
Reduce tumor size
questions.rationale: Treatment aims to reduce tumor size and manage symptoms.

questions.prompt: A patient with asthma has been prescribed a corticosteroid inhaler and a bronchodilator inhaler. How should these medications be administered?
options: The bronchodilator should be used, followed by the corticosteroid
The corticosteroid should be used, followed by the bronchodilator
Both inhalers should be used simultaneously
The order of administration does not matter
questions.rationale: The bronchodilator should be administered first to open the airways, allowing the corticosteroid to be more effectively delivered and absorbed.

questions.prompt: A nurse is providing discharge instructions to the parents of a child who has undergone chemotherapy. Which of the following instructions should be included?
options: "Your child should avoid crowds and people with infections."
"Your child can return to school and engage in physical activities."
"Your child should eat a diet high in raw fruits and vegetables."
"Your child can receive live virus vaccines."
questions.rationale: Children who have undergone chemotherapy have a suppressed immune system and are more susceptible to infections. They should avoid crowds and people with infections to minimize the risk of getting sick.

questions.prompt: A patient is frustrated and yelling about their pain management. What is the best response by the nurse?
options: "Yelling at me isn't going to help your situation."
"I understand you're in pain, let me notify your doctor."
"You need to calm down so we can discuss this rationally."
"Other patients are trying to rest, please lower your voice."
questions.rationale: Correct answer: "I understand you're in pain, let me notify your doctor." (Verified from eye and ear  QNS.docx and Saunders 9th Ed.).

questions.prompt: A nurse is caring for a patient with pneumonia. Which of the following interventions should the nurse prioritize?
options: Encourage ambulation
Administer antibiotics as prescribed
Maintain a patent airway
Promote fluid intake
questions.rationale: Maintaining a patent airway is the priority nursing intervention for a patient with pneumonia because pneumonia can cause mucus production that can obstruct the airway.

questions.prompt: A nurse is caring for a 3-year-old child with gastroenteritis. Which of the following signs would indicate dehydration?
options: Increased blood pressure
Decreased heart rate
Sunken fontanelle
Decreased urinary output
questions.rationale: Dehydration in children with gastroenteritis is a common complication due to fluid loss from vomiting and diarrhea. Decreased urinary output is a sign of dehydration. Increased blood pressure (option A) and decreased heart rate (option B) are not typical signs of dehydration. A sunken fontanelle (option C) could indicate dehydration, but it is not applicable in this case as the fontanelles are typically closed by age 2.

questions.prompt: A patient has been diagnosed with cataracts. Which of the following statements made by the patient indicates a need for further teaching?
options: "I will need to avoid bright lights."
"I will need surgery to remove the cataracts."
"I will be able to see better after the cataracts are removed."
"Cataracts can be prevented by wearing sunglasses."
questions.rationale: Correct answer: "Cataracts can be prevented by wearing sunglasses." (Verified from eye and ear  QNS.docx and Saunders 9th Ed.).

questions.prompt: A patient with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) has been admitted to the hospital. Which of the following findings would the nurse expect to observe during the assessment?
options: Decreased respiratory rate
Prolonged expiratory phase
Increased lung sounds
Absence of wheezing
questions.rationale: Patients with COPD often have difficulty exhaling, leading to a prolonged expiratory phase. The other options are not typical findings in COPD.

questions.prompt: A nurse is caring for several patients on a busy medical-surgical unit. Which of the following patients should the nurse prioritize?
options: A patient with a history of macular degeneration who needs assistance with meal setup
A patient with a hearing aid who needs the batteries changed
A patient with a history of stroke who is experiencing sudden vision changes
A patient with a new prescription for eyeglasses who needs education about care
questions.rationale: Correct answer: A patient with a history of stroke who is experiencing sudden vision changes (Verified from eye and ear  QNS.docx and Saunders 9th Ed.).

questions.prompt: A 2-year-old child presents with a "slapped cheek" appearance and a lacy rash on the body. What condition should the nurse suspect?
options: Measles
Roseola
Fifth disease
Scarlet fever
questions.rationale: Correct answer: Fifth disease (Verified from PAEDIATRIC QUESTIONS.docx and Saunders 9th Ed.).

questions.prompt: A nurse is educating a patient with COPD about the use of a metered-dose inhaler (MDI) with a spacer. Which of the following instructions should the nurse include?
options: Exhale completely before activating the MDI
Inhale quickly and forcefully through the spacer
Hold breath for 5 seconds after inhaling the medication
Rinse mouth with water immediately after using the MDI
questions.rationale: The patient should exhale completely to empty the lungs as much as possible before inhaling the medication. This allows for maximum distribution of the medication in the lungs.

questions.prompt: A patient with tuberculosis refuses to wear a mask when leaving the room for tests. What is the nurse's best response?
options: "You must wear the mask or you cannot leave the room."
"You are putting others at risk by not wearing a mask."
"I understand that the mask is uncomfortable, but it's necessary to prevent the spread of the disease."
"I will notify the physician that you are refusing to wear the mask."
questions.rationale: This response acknowledges the patient's feelings while emphasizing the need to prevent the spread of tuberculosis. It's a therapeutic communication technique that provides information and seeks to gain the patient's cooperation.

questions.prompt: A nurse is preparing to administer albuterol to a patient with asthma. Which of the following should the nurse monitor for as a potential side effect of this medication?
options: Bradycardia
Hypotension
Tachycardia
Hypoglycaemia
questions.rationale: Albuterol, a beta2-adrenergic agonist, can cause tachycardia as a side effect. It stimulates the beta2 receptors in the lungs causing bronchodilation, but it can also stimulate beta1 receptors in the heart causing increased heart rate.

questions.prompt: A 12-year-old child weighing 50 kg is ordered a medication at a dose of 5 mg/kg/day in 3 divided doses. How many milligrams of the medication will the nurse administer per dose?
options: 30 mg
50 mg
75 mg
83 mg
questions.rationale: Correct answer: 83 mg (Verified from PAEDIATRIC QUESTIONS.docx and Saunders 9th Ed.).

questions.prompt: A 6-year-old child weighing 20 kg is scheduled to receive a dose of medication. The medication is ordered at a dose of 5 mg/kg/dose every 8 hours. The medication comes in a concentration of 100 mg/5 mL. How many milliliters of medication will the nurse administer per dose?
options: 1 mL
2 mL
3 mL
5 mL
questions.rationale: Correct answer: 2 mL (Verified from PAEDIATRIC QUESTIONS.docx and Saunders 9th Ed.).

questions.prompt: A patient with Addison's disease is experiencing hypotension and dehydration. What is the nurse's first action?
options: Administer hydrocortisone
Check electrolyte levels
Encourage fluid intake
Provide oxygen therapy
questions.rationale: Hydrocortisone replaces deficient cortisol, helping manage hypotension and dehydration.

questions.prompt: A 1-year-old child weighing 10 kg is ordered amoxicillin at a dose of 25 mg/kg/day in 2 divided doses. How many milligrams of amoxicillin will the nurse administer for each dose?
options: 50 mg
75 mg
100 mg
125 mg
questions.rationale: Correct answer: 125 mg (Verified from PAEDIATRIC QUESTIONS.docx and Saunders 9th Ed.).
